Short summary: Establishes the LEAD for Kids Act, mandating AI systems intended for children to assess risk levels and adhere to regulations. Forms a board to oversee compliance, issue guidelines, and ensure AI doesn't adversely impact children. Imposes penalties for noncompliance.
Long summary:
Establishes the LEAD for Kids Standards Board to govern AI systems affecting children in California.

Requires AI developers to classify systems as "covered products" with risk assessments ranging from prohibited to low risk.

Mandates developers to register covered products and submit risk assessments by July 1, 2028.

Prohibits AI use that adversely impacts children's health, safety, or privacy without informed consent.

Requires companion chatbots and systems that assess emotional states or collect biometric data to receive additional scrutiny.

Mandates independent audits based on risk level and public incident reporting for adverse impacts.

Obligates deployers to prevent unauthorized child access and adhere to usage requirements that do not increase system risk.

Prohibits retaliation against employees reporting violations.

Allows the Attorney General to enforce violations with penalties, and provides a private right of action for harmed children.

Creates the LEAD for Kids AI Fund to support these regulatory activities.

Casual name: Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology
Short summary: Regulates facial recognition technology use in China, including through informed consent requirements, assessment requirements, storage and processing conditions, and certain outright prohibitions. Requires impact assessments and local filing for large volumes of facial recognition data. Delegates oversight and enforcement to cyberspace and public security authorities.
Long summary:
Regulates the use of facial recognition technology for processing facial information within China, ensuring compliance with relevant laws and ethical standards.

Exempts the use of facial recognition in research and development or algorithm training.

Requires a specific, necessary purpose for processing, with minimized impact on individual rights.

Obligates personal information processors to inform individuals transparently about processing activities, including purposes, methods, and rights.

Mandates obtaining consent separately for processing, with provision for withdrawal.

Requires parental consent for processing minors' facial information and formulating specific rules for handling such data.

Restricts storing facial information within devices unless consent or laws allow external transmission and limits retention to what is necessary.

Mandates conducting personal information protection impact assessments in advance and retaining assessment reports for three years.

Prohibits using facial recognition as the sole identity verification method if alternatives exist.

Requires filing procedures with local cyberspace administrations if information volume reaches 100,000 individuals.

Empowers cyberspace administrations and public security authorities to supervise, inspect, and handle complaints regarding facial recognition misuse.

Official name: Tennessee House Bill 2163 (Sexual Exploitation of Children)
Casual name: Tennessee HB 2163 (Sexual Exploitation of Children)
Short summary: Amends the definition of computer-generated images to include those modified by AI for sexual exploitation offenses. Defines "artificial intelligence" and "generative artificial intelligence" related to content creation. Takes effect on July 1, 2024.
Long summary:
Amends Tennessee Code to include computer-generated images created, adapted, or modified by artificial intelligence under the definition of materials related to the sexual exploitation of children.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions, influencing environments, or learning autonomously, developed in any context, including software or hardware, and solving tasks requiring human-like abilities.

Includes "generative artificial intelligence" as a system capable of creating new content or data, such as text, images, audio, or video when prompted.

Takes effect on July 1, 2024, for the purpose of public welfare.

Official name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs")
Casual name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs")
Short summary: Allocates $140 million for long-range unmanned aircraft systems and $75 million for autonomous maritime systems services. Allows procurement of Arctic Security Cutters by entities other than the Coast Guard. Requires compliance with reporting requirements and advance notification of cost changes.
Long summary:
Appropriates $140 million for long-range unmanned aircraft systems and related infrastructure to improve the US Coast Guard's capabilities. 

Allocates $180 million for maritime domain awareness equipment and services, including $75 million specifically for autonomous maritime systems. 

Allows, through 2030, for entities other than the Coast Guard to acquire, procure, or construct floating dry docks, provided they meet defined requirements. 

Limits design, planning, and engineering expenses to 15% of specified funding allocations for maintenance facilities. 

Exempts acquisitions funded under this act from sections 1131, 1132, and 1133 of title 14, United States Code. 

Mandates compliance with reporting requirements and submission of an expenditure plan to relevant Congressional committees.

Prohibits expenditure during any fiscal year if the Coast Guard is non-compliant with specified sections of title 14, United States Code. 

Requires prior notification to Congress before procurement actions affecting cost or timelines.

Casual name: Child Exploitation and AI Commission Act
Short summary: Establishes a Commission of Experts to evaluate the existing capabilities of law enforcement to detect and prosecute child exploitation crimes involving AI, and recommend solutions to any barriers that the may face in the identification and prosecution of these crimes
Long summary:
Establishes the Commission of Experts on Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence to investigate and recommend solutions for the prevention, detection, and prosecution of child exploitation crimes involving AI.

Directs the Commission to assess the role of AI in child exploitation and evaluate law enforcement's current capabilities to detect and prosecute such crimes.

Requires the Commission to recommend statutory or constitutional amendments to address obstacles to prosecution identified by the Commission and enhance law enforcement's ability to combat AI-facilitated child exploitation.

Mandates the Commission to submit to Congress interim reports as needed and a final report within two years of member appointments.

Details membership of the Commission as composed of 13 appointed experts from various fields, and outlines guidelines on membership qualifications and operational procedures of the commission.

Empowers the Commission to conduct its duties, including to hold hearings, obtain official data, and utilize various support services for its operations.

Official name: HR 4518 Cooper Davis and Devin Norring Act 2025 (Requires communication service and remote computing providers to report certain controlled substances violations)
Casual name: HR 4518 Cooper Davis and Devin Norring Act 2025
Short summary: Require electronic communication and remote computing service providers to report controlled substances violations, discovered via algorithms or human moderation, to the Attorney General. Specify duties, reporting, preservation, and penalties related to violations, excluding broadband and text messaging services.
Long summary:
Amends the Controlled Substances Act to require electronic communication and remote computing service providers to report certain controlled substances violations to the Attorney General.

Requires providers to report known instances of unlawful activities involving fentanyl, methamphetamine, counterfeit substances, or unauthorized prescription drugs within 60 days, including details on how violations were discovered, whether through human or AI methods such as algorithms and machine learning.

Instructs the Attorney General to review and act on reports, potentially involving other law enforcement agencies in investigations.

Obligates the Attorney General to minimize data storage and ensure privacy by encrypting communications and prohibiting user monitoring.

Outlines penalties for non-compliance and false reporting.

Exempts broadband internet and text messaging services from these requirements.

Mandates an annual report from the Attorney General summarizing the number and outcomes of reports received.

Official name: HR 4503 ePermit Act 2025 (Environmental reviews and authorizations through the use of digital platforms)
Casual name: HR 4503 ePermit Act 2025
Short summary: Requires the Chair of the Council on Environmental Quality to develop data standards and prototype tools using AI to enhance environmental reviews and authorizations. Instructs federal agencies to implement these standards and tools, focusing on automation, transparency, and data interoperability.
Long summary:
Establishes data standards for environmental reviews, requiring the Chair of the Council on Environmental Quality, in consultation with relevant entities, to design these standards to reduce redundant reviews and improve data interoperability between federal agencies.

Requires development of prototype tools for environmental reviews to enhance data exchange, management, and transparency.

Directs the Chair to publish guidance for implementing data standards and minimum functional requirements to aid automation and efficiency.

Obligates federal agencies to assess existing capabilities and begin implementation of standards and tools within specific timeframes.

Creates a unified interagency data system with an interactive, cloud-based authorization portal to streamline review processes, ensure vendor-neutral data exchange, and provide public accessibility to non-sensitive data.

Includes provisions for cybersecurity and congressional oversight, ensuring the integration and compliance of the system with existing laws and security measures.

Official name: HR 4965 Counseling for Career Choice Act 2025 (Amend the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to expand educational opportunities, including using AI)
Casual name: HR 4965 Counseling for Career Choice Act 2025
Short summary: Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to include using artificial intelligence in career counseling. Encourages leveraging AI to support career development, enhancing career counseling activities, and evaluating educational outcomes.
Long summary:
Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to enhance career counseling opportunities.

Requires career guidance and school counseling programs to identify regional workforce trends with state and regional entities.

Develops and implements processes for school counselors to access workforce trend information.

Provides school counselors with resources to deliver relevant career and postsecondary education advice using current workforce data and financial aid assistance.

Encourages professional development for counselors through certification programs, potentially with industry associations.

Facilitates partnerships with one-stop centers, including co-locating them in high schools or assisting counselors with job fairs.

Leverages emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to support career development and counseling.

Evaluates outcomes of individuals served by counseling programs.

Official name: HR 4661 Autonomous Mobility Ensuring Regulation, Innovation, Commerce, and Advancement Driving Reliability in Vehicle Efficiency and Safety Act 2025
Casual name: HR 4661 AMERICA DRIVES Act 2025
Short summary: Amends title 49 to allow Level 4 and 5 ADS-equipped commercial vehicles to operate without a human driver. Instructs the Secretary of Transportation to update regulations by 2027 for ADS integration. Prohibits burdensome regulations on ADS-operated vehicles.
Long summary:
Amends title 49, United States Code, to preempt State laws requiring a human occupant in automated driving systems-equipped commercial motor vehicles.

Permits operation of Level 4 or Level 5 ADS-equipped vehicles in interstate commerce without a human driver on board or a remote human driver.

Directs the Secretary of Transportation to issue necessary regulations and to update sections 350-399 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations by September 30, 2027, to integrate ADS into commercial vehicle operations.

Precludes regulations that unduly burden motor carriers operating ADS-equipped vehicles.

Excludes ADS technologies from width calculations under Section 31113.

Defines "remote driver" and "remote assistance" for regulatory purposes.

Instructs application of specific regulations to include cab-mounted warning beacons as a permissible warning device.

Official name: HR 4980 Battling Infections Transmitted by Ticks and Exposure Act 2025
Casual name: HR 4980 BITE Act 2025
Short summary: Establishes an AI-enhanced early warning system predicting vector-borne disease activity using weather, habitat, and wildlife data. Delivers real-time risk alerts. Instructs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement this system within a national vector-borne disease prevention framework.
Long summary:
Establishes the Secretary of Health and Human Services' responsibility to create a comprehensive national vector-borne disease prevention system.

Incorporates an artificial intelligence-enhanced early warning system to predict disease activity using weather, habitat, and wildlife data, and to deliver real-time, location-based risk alerts.

Integrates data reporting with human, animal, and environmental data through a professional vector identification service.

Includes insurance claims surveillance to detect outbreaks earlier than traditional methods and syndromic surveillance of emergency room visits for vector-borne symptoms.

Aims for comprehensive public education by delivering targeted prevention messaging and collaborating with schools, workplaces, media, and community organizations.

Sets a national strategic alignment goal of reducing Lyme disease by 25 percent by 2035 and enhancing military readiness through early detection and ecosystem health.

Official name: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback)
Casual name: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback)
Short summary: Establishes ethics review committees for S&T activities, including AI, to assess ethical risks. Requires committees to follow principles of independence and transparency and create emergency review procedures designed to evaluate high-risk AI activities needed in urgent situations.
Long summary:
Establishes that work units engaged in sensitive areas, including AI, must form ethics committees to conduct thorough ethical reviews of S&T activities.

Requires these reviews to ensure AI activities comply with ethics principles, such as fairness and inclusivity.

Stipulates review committees to include diverse experts and provide training on ethics reviews.

Mandates reviews of AI systems and algorithms adhere to national data security and ethical norms, ensuring transparency and reliability.

Grants committees the authority to approve, revise, or reject AI projects based on ethical evaluations.

Introduces simplified emergency review procedures for low-risk or urgent situations, with detailed conditions.

Calls for procedures to handle violations within AI ethics reviews, including potential penalties.

Insists on a national ethics management registry for committee activities and checklisted high-risk AI activities.

Implies that the Ministry of Science and Technology oversees interpretation and enforcement of these measures, which include significant provisions for governance of AI research and its ethical implications.

Casual name: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
Short summary: Instructs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop, update, and disseminate AI resources for small businesses. Coordinates with the Small Business Administration for distribution. Requires periodic review and reporting to Congress on AI resource development and usage.
Long summary:
Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop or identify and disseminate resources for small businesses to utilize artificial intelligence, subject to appropriation availability.

Ensures these resources include technical standards, best practices, and methodologies tailored to small businesses, promoting basic AI understanding and adoption, and are technology-neutral, based on international standards where applicable.

Mandates a review and updating of resources every two years.

Coordinates resource dissemination with the Small Business Administration.

Specifies resources as voluntary for small businesses.

Requires a report to be submitted to relevant Congressional Committees within four years, detailing resource development and updates, user feedback, and recommendations for further congressional actions to support AI utilization by small businesses.

Official name: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024
Casual name: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act
Short summary: Mandates the establishment of an interagency Federal Export Enforcement Coordination Center to coordinate U.S. export control enforcement, focusing on AI and other sensitive technologies; directs the Center to develop best practices for combatting unlawful transshipment and diversion of exports; authorizes an appropriation of $25 million for fiscal year 2025 to establish the Center.
Long summary:
Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish an interagency Federal Export Enforcement Coordination Center to coordinate export control enforcement among various federal departments and agencies.

Focuses the Center's efforts on sensitive technologies, including advanced artificial intelligence capabilities, semiconductors, and quantum technology.

Directs the Center to develop best practices and disseminate actionable information to the private sector about transshipment and diversion risks.

Requires the Director of the Center to submit reports to Congress on the value and logistics of posting U.S. law enforcement officials abroad and hosting foreign officials at the Center to enhance export control enforcement. 

Authorizes an appropriation of $25 million for fiscal year 2025 for the establishment of the Center.

Casual name: Memo 25-22  (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government)
Collections: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
Short summary: Directs Federal agencies to acquire AI systems in such a way that enhances efficiency, competitive procurement, and mitigates vendor lock-in risks at the lowest cost to the taxpayer. Requires policy updates for privacy, intellectual property, and data management while also mandating interagency collaboration.
Long summary:
Promotes the competitive American AI marketplace by mandating federal agencies to procure AI systems that enhance efficiency and mission effectiveness while avoiding dependence on single vendors.

Ensures taxpayer dollars are safeguarded by tracking AI performance and managing risks as outlined in Executive Order 13960.

Mandates the protection of privacy and intellectual property, emphasizing compliance with federal law and policy.

Excludes certain AI acquisitions and activities, such as national security systems and incidental AI use by contractors.

Requires GSA to develop AI acquisition guides within 100 days and establish a shared repository of best practices within 200 days.

Long summary:

Requires open competition to acquire AI-enabled inspection technologies.

Obliges U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to submit monthly expenditure plans for procuring and deploying autonomous systems, including timelines and sustainment costs.

Mandates CBP quarterly updates on the impact of border security technologies, including AI, on CBP performance, capabilities, and workforce requirements.

Requires the Under Secretary for Management at DHS to submit monthly expenditure and hiring plans for allocated funds until the funds are expended; prohibits obligation of funds before submission of such plans.

Casual name: Testing at Residence Telehealth Act, Sec. 2 ("Tests and Assistive Telehealth Consultations Demonstration")
Short summary: Establishes a Value-Based Insurance Design Model demonstration program to provide telehealth consultations and home care to beneficiaries enrolled in eligible Medicare Advantage (MA) plans; defines eligible MA plans to include those that cover AI-enabled tests; establishes a grant program for state Medicaid programs to cover AI-enabled medical tests.
Long summary:

Defines "eligible MA plans" to include those that cover AI-enabled tests and devices.

Limits the VBID program to a maximum of 25 MA plans, with at least 10 plans serving rural or underserved areas.

Requires the VBID program to be implemented by the second January after the enactment of the bill and to operate for five years, with the potential for extension and expansion.

Mandates an independent, third-party evaluation of the VBID demonstration program, including an assessment of how the program has improved patient care and quality of life and addressed disparities for underserved populations.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to administer a grant program for state Medicaid programs to cover AI-enabled tests, with grants awarded to 5-10 states or territories for a 4-year period, not exceeding $12 million per state.

Implements data security measures to protect training and operational data, ensuring privacy and accuracy.

Enhances infrastructure security through regular penetration tests and incident response protocols.

Requires transparency in AI model capabilities, limitations, and risk disclosures.

Advances research in AI safety and security, addressing potential biases and risks in frontier applications.

Official name: Oklahoma House Bill 1916
Casual name: Oklahoma Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act
Short summary: Enacts the "Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act," requiring the classification of AI systems in Oklahoma by risk level, mandating oversight and audits for high-risk AI systems. Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council to enforce compliance, oversee innovation programs, and guide ethical AI testing and development.
Long summary:
Enacts the "Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act," mandating comprehensive governance structures for AI deployment in Oklahoma and requiring classification of all AI systems by risk level based on their potential impact on safety, civil liberties, and fundamental rights.

Prohibits the development and deployment of Unacceptable Risk AI systems, such as social scoring or AI-driven misinformation, while imposing strict oversight, audits, and transparency requirements on high-risk systems.

Requires deployers to assess AI systems for biases, safety risks, and rights violations before deployment, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure qualified human oversight that can override system decisions.

Requires public notification and appeal mechanisms when high-risk AI systems are used to make decisions that impact individuals, ensuring transparency and recourse.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council (AI Council) to regulate ethical AI use, including the AI Regulatory Sandbox Program and Workforce Development Program, to allow controlled testing of AI systems. 

Launches the AI Workforce Development Program to expand AI literacy and skills in underserved communities, prioritizing affordable training through grants to small businesses and educational institutions.

Permits the AI Council to issue penalties for noncompliance and requires deployers to disclose related incidents.

Long summary:
Directs all Executive Branch departments and agencies to adopt AI by accelerating AI use and innovation while ensuring responsible deployment and governance.  

Requires removal of barriers to AI innovation, focusing on delivering value for taxpayers and improving public services.  

Instructs agencies to develop and share AI strategies, prioritize American AI products, and enhance workforce AI readiness.  

Directs agencies to designate a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) to oversee AI efforts and improve public accountability.  

Mandates implementation of minimum risk management practices for high-impact AI and provides guidance on AI governance, including creating AI impact assessments and ensuring human oversight.  

Encourages sharing and reusing of AI resources across federal agencies to prevent redundancy and foster collaboration.  

Implements public trust in AI use by requiring performance monitoring and mechanisms for public consultation and feedback.

Official name: Digital Evaluation for Tax Enforcement and Compliance Tracking Act of 2025
Casual name: DETECT Act of 2025
Short summary: Requires the Comptroller General to submit a report to Congress within 180 days on the potential for artificial intelligence to assist the IRS in detecting tax fraud.
Long summary:
Requires the Comptroller General to submit a report to the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Senate Committee on Finance.

Instructs the report to focus on the potential of artificial intelligence to assist the IRS in detecting tax fraud.

Sets a deadline of 180 days from the enactment of the Act for the submission of this report.

Official name: South Dakota 2024 Senate Bill 79
Casual name: South Dakota SB 79 (Child Pornography)
Short summary: Defines "computer-generated child pornography" to include AI-generated images indistinguishable from minors in sexual acts. Criminalizes possession, distribution, and manufacturing of such content, with severe felony penalties. Prohibits defenses based on consent or age mistake. Recognizes mitigating sentencing circumstances.
Long summary:
Defines "computer-generated child pornography" to include AI-generated depictions indistinguishable from actual minors engaged in prohibited sexual acts.

Criminalizes possession, distribution, and manufacture of child pornography, including AI-generated content, with varying felony classes and mandatory minimum sentences for first and subsequent offenses.

Prohibits defenses based on consent or mistaken age, but allows an affirmative defense if the depiction is solely of the person charged.

Mandates court assessments for convicted individuals and allows sentence mitigation in specific circumstances.

Requires prior out-of-state convictions for similar offenses to be considered in determining repeat offenses.

Specifies that certain materials with serious value are exempt from these prohibitions.

Incorporates offenses involving child pornography into the definitions of sex crimes, impacting registration and sentencing.

Addresses juvenile sexting, deeming it a misdemeanor if minors distribute or possess nude images or participate in prohibited acts using digital media.

Official name: California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations
Casual name: CPPA Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations
Short summary: Requires risk assessments for processing personal information with AI, especially when impacting significant consumer decisions or involving extensive profiling. Mandates transparency and consumer rights to opt-out of automated decision making technology, especially when such automated decision making tools are used to render significant decisions surrounding the status of an employee, candidate or other class of individual.
Long summary:
Mandates businesses to conduct risk assessments for using AI and automated decision-making technology when handling consumer data, especially for decisions impacting financial, employment, or educational opportunities.

Requires transparency through Pre-use Notices for consumers, detailing the use of AI in decision-making and providing opt-out or appeal options.

Specifies exceptions where consumers cannot opt-out, mainly when processing is necessary for service, or on the basis of exceptions grounded in prevention of fraud, with provisions for human review upon request.

Instructs businesses to ensure AI does not discriminate against protected classes through evaluations and safeguards.

Obliges businesses to disclose AI processes upon consumer request and prohibits retaliatory actions against consumers exercising their rights in accordance with the CCPA.

Mandates comprehensive documentation and regular updates for risk assessments, maintaining consumer privacy as a priority.

Official name: HR 4155 American Agricultural Security Research Act of 2025
Casual name: HR 4155 Agricultural Security Research Act of 2025
Short summary: Establishes AI-focused centers for agricultural research and education. Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to recognize centers on digital agriculture, including AI and remote sensing systems. Provides grants for research improving agricultural biosecurity and cybersecurity.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to recognize centers of excellence in several areas, including digital agriculture, which focuses on developing AI and remote sensing systems.

Instructs host institutions to partner with entities like the Agricultural Research Service to enhance research coordination and fill program gaps.

Authorizes up to $10 million annually from 2026 to 2030 for implementing these centers.

Establishes a grant program to protect the U.S. food and agriculture system from cybersecurity threats, awarding grants for research or development in agricultural biosecurity and cybersecurity.

Specifies eligible grant recipients, such as universities and research institutions.

Encourages research, teaching programs, and facility upgrades to enhance biosecurity and cybersecurity expertise, emphasizing the importance of trained individuals and protective infrastructures.

Authorizes an additional $10 million annually from 2026 to 2030 for the grant program.

Official name: HR 4141 Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act 2025
Casual name: HR 4141 Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act 2025
Short summary: Directs the Under Secretary to leverage AI and machine learning to optimize computing for NOAA's critical missions. Establishes centers of excellence for AI-enabled computing. Requires a strategic plan addressing NOAA's high-performance computing needs, including AI utilization and development timelines.
Long summary:
Amends the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act to require the Under Secretary to utilize AI and machine learning for NOAA's missions.

Authorizes the establishment of Centers of Excellence to enhance AI and machine learning computing capacities through public-private partnerships and resource development.

Permits exploration of quantum computing to improve weather prediction accuracy.

Allows multi-year contracts to support high-performance computing infrastructure and cloud systems.

Mandates a report within two years, in collaboration with the Secretary of Energy, to evaluate high-resolution weather forecast value and computing needs.

Requires a public 10-year strategic plan outlining NOAA's high-performance computing and data management needs, updated every five years until 2035.

Involves public feedback in plan development and annual briefings to Congress on plan progress, highlighting computing infrastructure and technology advancements for NOAA.

Official name: HR 4419 Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act 2025
Casual name: HR 4419 AV Accessibility Act 2025
Short summary: Prohibits states from issuing licenses for Level 4 or 5 ADS-equipped vehicles in a discriminatory manner against individuals with disabilities. Instructs the Secretary of Transportation to conduct a study on accessible infrastructure for these vehicles.
Long summary:
Prohibits states from issuing motor vehicle operator's licenses for Level 4 or Level 5 ADS-equipped vehicles in a manner that discriminates against individuals with disabilities.

Requires the adherence to title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act in licensing practices for such vehicles.

Instructs the Secretary of Transportation to collaborate with the National Academies on a study to assess public transportation infrastructure improvements for accessibility to ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicles.

Tasks the study with identifying options to enhance safe access for individuals with disabilities, including technological solutions and dedicated zones for pickup and drop-off.

Authorizes the appropriation of $5,000,000 for the accessible infrastructure study, available until expended.

Official name: HR 4473 United States-Israel Bilateral Innovation for Research and Development in Health Act of 2025
Casual name: HR 4473 BIRD Health Act of 2025
Short summary: Establishes the BIRD Health Program to foster U.S.-Israel collaboration on healthcare technologies, including AI-driven diagnostics. Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to coordinate efforts, allocate funding, and support innovation in AI health applications.
Long summary:
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a bilateral research and innovation program with Israel, called the BIRD Health Program, focused on healthcare collaboration.

Requires the program to specifically promote joint research and development projects, including those using artificial intelligence for healthcare applications.

Specifies that the BIRD Health Program will be governed by both the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the Israeli Ministry of Health.

Provides funding for research in telemedicine, digital health, disease prevention, and biological product manufacturing, emphasizing AI-driven diagnostics.

Stipulates $10 million annually for fiscal years 2026 to 2032 for the program, administered through the BIRD Foundation.

Directs submission of annual reports to Congress on the program's impact, economic benefits, and recommendations, with a comprehensive review every three years.

Defines "health technology" to include AI-driven diagnostics.

Official name: Detection Equipment and Technology Evaluation to Counter the Threat of Fentanyl and Xylazine Act of 2024
Casual name: DETECT Fentanyl and Xylazine Act of 2024
Short summary: Amends the Homeland Security Act to enhance drug detection capabilities using AI, requiring research and development of equipment for law enforcement. Directs adherence to AI risk management guidelines and prioritization based on DEA threat reports.
Long summary:
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to enhance the detection and disruption of drugs like fentanyl and xylazine using advanced technologies.

Mandates research and development of equipment for drug detection and trafficking disruption, emphasizing minimal handling and separation of complex mixtures.

Incorporates machine learning and artificial intelligence to predict controlled substance analogues and new psychoactive substances.

Requires the Under Secretary for Science and Technology to adhere to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or its successor.

Establishes research and evaluation priorities using the latest information from reports on drug threats by the Drug Enforcement Administration.

Ensures federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies have access to improved detection technologies.

Official name: Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection)
Casual name: Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection)
Short summary: Commits to a phased, responsible approach to AI scaling, encompassing pre-deployment safety evaluations, post-launch monitoring, and participation in global governance efforts. Requires rigorous model evaluations, red teaming, data input controls, and security measures, and supports research on AI risks and standardization of AI-generated content identification.
Long summary:
Commits Inflection to a disciplined, phased approach to scaling AI models, emphasizing pre-deployment safety, post-launch monitoring, and global governance.

Requires robust evaluations and third-party red-teaming before public launch to ensure models do not provide harmful information or engage in discriminatory conduct.

Implements strict data input controls and audits, involving executive review and legal evaluations of training data for compliance with legal and ethical standards.

Ensures high-level security controls to prevent unauthorized access and misuse of AI models, including internal restrictions and a bug bounty program, and promotes a cross-industry information sharing effort.

Maintains around-the-clock monitoring to detect and mitigate model misuse, employing frontier AI to enhance situational awareness.

Publishes model capabilities and limitations, supporting transparency and enabling risk assessment by users and regulators.

Advocates for standardized vulnerability reporting structures and participates in a pilot bug bounty program to proactively identify vulnerabilities.

Prioritizes research on AI risks and supports the creation of an International Panel on AI Safety.

Promotes cross-industry collaboration for identifying AI-generated material, focusing on child safety and standardized watermarking.

Official name: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
Casual name: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
Short summary: Requires the Chief Data Officer (CDO) Council to identify procedures that support the reliable and secure adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) across federal agencies and adds a Chief AI Officer representative to the Council. Mandates reports and guidance on AI data governance best practices, including prioritizing AI use cases, managing training data transparency, and ensuring the privacy and security of synthetic data.
Long summary:
Defines "artificial intelligence" (AI) and establishes that data governance encompasses ensuring data privacy and security.

Requires the Chief Data Officer (CDO) Council to identify procedures that support the reliable and secure adoption of AI across agencies.

Mandates the appointment of a representative from among Chief AI Officers to the CDO Council.

Obligates the Council to submit reports recommending data governance policies for AI, including guidelines for ensuring training data protects privacy and mitigates bias.

Instructs the Council to recommend policies for AI data ownership, pre-procurement error reviews, and training data transparency.

Requires recommendations on mitigating the privacy and security risks associated with synthetic data generation and use.

Authorizes the Director of the Office of Electronic Government to issue agency guidance based on the CDO Council's reports.

Mandates an annual report to Congress clarifying the roles, collaboration opportunities, and needed skills of CDOs in AI governance.

Requires a Comptroller General evaluation of the Council's effectiveness and sunsets the amendments seven years after enactment.

Official name: Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act
Casual name: DETOUR Act
Short summary: Prohibits large online operators from designing user interfaces that impair user autonomy or encourage compulsive usage; requires affirmative express consent for certain research involving user data and mandates disclosure of such research. Establishes independent review boards and empowers the FTC to enforce compliance.
Long summary:
Prohibits large online operators from manipulating user interfaces to obscure, subvert, or impair user autonomy, decision making, or consent.

Requires affirmative express consent from users for covered research and prohibits manipulation aimed at children or teens to encourage compulsive usage.

Mandates large online operators to disclose the purpose of covered research to users every 90 days and ensure transparency.

Obligates large online operators to establish independent review boards to oversee user interface design and research, ensuring compliance and preventing exploitative practices.

Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop resources for user interface design promoting user autonomy, choice, and decision making.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance, establish regulations for independent review boards, and define acceptable conduct for large online operators.

Provides safe harbor for operators acting in good faith per established guidelines.

Official name: Massachusetts HD 396 (2025-2026)
Casual name: Massachusetts HD396 (An Act to ensure accountability and transparency in artificial intelligence systems)
Short summary: Establishes AI accountability and consumer protection laws in Massachusetts. Requires developers to mitigate algorithmic discrimination risks and disclose them. Mandates deployers implement risk management for high-risk AI. Enforces corporate AI disclosure and consumer notification. Grants authority to Attorney General for enforcement.
Long summary:
Establishes Chapter 93M regarding AI accountability and consumer protection in Massachusetts, defining key terms such as algorithmic discrimination and high-risk AI systems. 

Mandates developers to identify, mitigate, and disclose risks of algorithmic discrimination, and requires public summaries of AI systems and biases.

Compels deployers of high-risk AI systems to implement risk management programs and conduct annual impact assessments, with mandatory consumer notifications on consequential AI decisions.

Requires corporations to disclose their use of AI in consumer targeting and behavior influence, ensuring transparency and consumer rights protection.

Exempts small businesses, low-risk systems, and federally compliant entities from certain provisions.

Empowers the Attorney General to enforce regulations, categorizing violations under unfair trade practices, while providing a defense for proactive compliance.

Permits rulemaking authority for the Attorney General to set compliance and notification standards and mandates a public education campaign on AI consumer rights. 

Specifies varying effective dates for sections within 180 days to one year post-passage.

Official name: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment for the Americas"), Sec. 255 ("Transformational Energy Development")
Casual name: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment"), Sec. 255 ("Energy Development")
Short summary: Mandates the creation of a Chief Energy Office at the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and an Office of Energy at the Export-Import Bank of the U.S. (EXIM) to support transformational energy projects, including the use of AI to improve energy efficiency and energy infrastructure.
Long summary:
Amends the BUILD Act of 2018 to define "transformational energy technology," including the use of AI to improve energy efficiency and energy infrastructure.

Requires the appointment of a Chief Energy Officer at DFC to promote transformational energy technology projects and ensure at least 30% of DFC support targets such projects.

Establishes an Office of Energy at EXIM to promote eligible technologies, including AI applications to improve energy efficiency and energy infrastructure.

Requires annual DFC and EXIM reports on transformational energy technology projects.

Mandates the creation of a Joint Energy Export, Development, and Trade Database of transformational energy technology projects that receive support from various federal agencies.

Requires quarterly interagency meetings to review the database and identify areas for collaboration.

Requires quarterly reports on the database to relevant congressional committees.

Official name: California Senate Bill 53
Casual name: California SB 53 September 2025 (Artificial intelligence models: large developers)
Collections: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
Short summary: Requires large frontier developers to implement and publish frontier AI frameworks, assess catastrophic risks, and publish transparency reports; requires the Office of Emergency Services to establish reporting mechanisms for critical safety incidents and catastrophic risk assessments; establishes a consortium to develop a framework for the creation of CalCompute; creates civil penalties for violations of this chapter.
Long summary:
Defines terms for the purposes of this chapter, including catastrophic risk and critical safety incident.

Requires large frontier developers to implement and publish frontier AI frameworks, publish transparency reports, and disclose assessments of catastrophic risks to the Office of Emergency Services.

Instructs the Office of Emergency Services to establish a critical safety incident reporting mechanism and a mechanism for frontier developers to submit summaries of catastrophic risk assessments; mandates the disclosure of critical safety incidents that pose an imminent risk of death or serious injury within 24 hours. 

Tasks the Office of Emergency Services, beginning in 2027, to annually produce and submit a report with anonymized and aggregated information regarding critical safety incidents to the Legislature and Governor.

Creates a civil penalty of up to $1,000,000 for violations of this chapter, specifically the failure of a frontier developer to report a safety incident or comply with their own frontier AI framework.

Creates a 14-member consortium to develop a framework for the creation of CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster that will advance the development and deployment of safe and equitable AI. 

Prohibits frontier developers from preventing, or retaliating against, covered employees who disclose information about catastrophic risks or violations of the Business and Professions Code.

Provides remedies for violations of this section, and explains how courts should handle cases regarding disclosures made by covered employees.

Casual name: National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies)
Short summary: Establishes a program to improve federal efforts to reduce wildland fire risks; requires the program to include a wildland fire airspace operations system involving autonomous capabilities.
Long summary:
Mandates the creation of a National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program to reduce losses of life and property from wildland fires through a coordinated federal effort.

Requires the NASA Administrator, in collaboration with other relevant agencies and stakeholders, to establish a program to develop a wildland fire airspace operations system, including autonomous capabilities, to monitor and mitigate wildland fires.

Official name: 21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act")
Casual name: 21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications")
Short summary: Prohibits entities from distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary-controlled applications in the U.S. Requires user data portability before prohibition. Allows civil penalties for violations. Permits exemptions for qualified divestitures and necessary services. Grants judicial review in D.C. Circuit.
Long summary:
Prohibits entities from distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary controlled applications within the U.S.

Requires data portability for users before prohibitions apply, enabling users to access their data in a machine-readable format.

Exempts applications undergoing "qualified divestiture" from prohibitions.

Enforces penalties up to $5,000 per user for distribution violations and $500 per user for data portability violations.

Mandates the Attorney General to investigate and enforce compliance through civil penalties or court actions.

Defines "foreign adversary controlled applications" and "qualified divestiture" to ensure clarity in application and exemptions.

Grants judicial review exclusively to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, with specified time limits for challenges.

Official name: Contraband Awareness Technology Catches Harmful Fentanyl Act
Casual name: CATCH Fentanyl Act
Short summary: Establishes pilot projects for testing AI and other technology enhancements to improve contraband detection at U.S. land ports of entry. Requires assessments of technology effectiveness, integration, and cost. Involves private sector input and mandates reporting to Congress on outcomes and recommendations no later than three years from the implementation of the Act.
Long summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the CBP Innovation Team, to establish pilot projects within one year to test and assess technologies enhancing nonintrusive inspection systems at land ports of entry.

Enacts pilot programs requiring testing of at least five types technology types, including at least one of the technologies from the following categories: artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum information sciences in order to detect contraband such as  illegal drugs, and human cargo.

Identifies effective enhancements based on detection accuracy, efficiency, integration capability, cost, safety, and ease of integration with existing systems.

Allows private sector input on commercially viable technologies.

Sets termination of pilot projects five years post-enactment.

Requires reporting to Congress (the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate) within three years and after project termination, detailing effectiveness, recommendations, cost plans, and performance analysis of tested technologies. 

Addresses privacy and civil rights concerns; mandates a report to be drafted by the DHS Privacy officer and Civil Liberties Officer, in consultation with the CBP Innovation and  to be delivered to the Committee on Homeland Security and Government Affairs of the Senate no later than 180 days after pilot program termination.

Requires the Under Secretary of the Office of Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response to develop a plan to ensure that loans and other incentives to encourage domestic manufacturing serve the greatest needs of critical industries, including AI.

Establishes a fund in the U.S. Treasury for supply chain resilience for critical industries, including AI.

Short summary: Requires the Secretary of State to report on the implementation of the AUKUS partnership, including efforts to enhance collaboration on AI.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, and Energy, to submit a report to relevant congressional committees on interagency efforts to implement the advanced capabilities pillar of the AUKUS partnership.

Requires the report to assess the efforts of AUKUS partners to enhance collaboration on AI.

Obligates the President to brief congressional committees annually for seven years on AUKUS implementation status, including the status of collaboration on AI and other advanced defense capabilities.

Long summary:
Requires the Chairman of the Board of Veterans Appeals to identify common legal or factual questions that the Board considers when reviewing appeals.

Casual name: Virginia HB2094 (High-Risk Artificial Intelligence Developer And Deployer Act)

Short summary: Establishes operating standards for developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems, including mandatory risk management and impact assessments. Requires disclosures of potential algorithmic discrimination risks.
Long summary:
Enacts stringent frameworks for the development and deployment of high-risk AI systems in Virginia.

Defines consequential decisions as those which may affect access to the justice system, education, employment, and financial or other such services.

Defines high-risk AI systems as those used in a consequential decision, excluding systems restricted to narrows tasks, pattern detection, and human assistance.

Mandates developers to disclose intended uses, data inputs, potential risks of algorithmic discrimination, and performance evaluations to deployers.

Requires deployers to implement risk management policies, conduct pre and post deployment impact assessments, and disclose AI system interactions to consumers, especially when making consequential decisions.

Establishes a duty of care for developers and deployers to protect against algorithmic discrimination.

Outlines civil penalties for violations, including a fine up to $1,000, with enforcement authority granted exclusively to the Attorney General.

Provides exemptions for various sectors and situations, including federal compliance and actions in the public interest.

Allows for updates post-modification of AI systems and sets guidelines for consumer notifications and appeal processes in case of adverse decisions due to AI use.

Casual name: Workforce of the Future Act of 2024
Short summary: Requires a report on AI's impact on the U.S. workforce and recommendations for educating and upskilling workers for an AI economy. Directs the Secretaries of Education and Labor to award grants for expanding AI and technology education from pre-K through high school and updating workforce AI skills development, respectively.
Long summary:
Mandates the preparation of reports by the Secretary of Labor, the National Science Foundation, and the Secretary of Education on AI's workforce impact, identifying data needs, affected industries, and opportunities for stakeholder influence.

Authorizes the Department of Education to award grants to enhance emerging and advanced technology education from prekindergarten through grade 12, with provisions for improving inclusivity for underrepresented communities.

Requires the Department of Labor to grant funds for upskilling workers in industries significantly impacted by AI, promoting lifelong learning and skill certifications.

Prescribes continuous evaluation and monitoring of grant-funded activities, with a focus on sustaining project activities post-grant.

Demands biannual reporting by grantees on fund usage, disaggregated by demographic factors, and a comprehensive report to Congress within five years.

Amends existing education laws to integrate emerging technology education data, emphasizing competency in AI-related skills among students.

Official name: Colorado SB 25B-008 (Tech-Neutral Anti-Discrimination Clarification Act 2025)
Casual name: Colorado SB 25B-008 (Tech-Neutral Anti-Discrimination Clarification Act 2025)
Short summary: Prohibits discrimination utilizing AI or digital technologies. Specifies liability for creators if they intentionally engage in discriminatory conduct. Clarifies non-exclusivity of technological terms. Confirms applicability of existing civil rights laws to AI-enabled actions. Effective January 1, 2026.
Long summary:
Repeals and reenacts Colorado's anti-discrimination statutes to prohibit discrimination facilitated by digital technologies, including AI.

Clarifies that advances in AI and other technologies do not provide a legal excuse for discriminatory practices.

Affirms that digital mechanisms used for illegal discrimination do not grant legal immunity.

Ensures civil rights laws apply consistently across all technologies without privileging any method.

Prohibits discrimination in Colorado through digital, automated, or AI processes.

Specifies illustrative terms for digital processes, covering current and future technologies.

Limits liability for technology creators, publishers, or distributors to intentional or knowing facilitation of discrimination.

Maintains existing burdens of proof, defenses, and remedies for discrimination claims.

Sets the act's effective date as January 1, 2026, contingent on potential referendum outcomes.

Applies the act to conduct occurring on or after its effective date.

Official name: HR 6304 AI for America Act 2025 (A national strategy for AI that promotes American leadership, removes regulatory barriers, and ensures data are free from security risks and ideological bias)
Casual name: HR 6304 AI for America Act 2025
Short summary: Directs the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy to submit a national AI action plan by 2027. Requires identification of regulatory barriers in specific sectors. Tasks NIST with reporting on AI security risks and bias prevention.
Long summary:
Codifies a national strategy to promote American leadership in artificial intelligence, addressing regulatory barriers and ensuring data security and impartiality.

Directs the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, in coordination with relevant agencies, to submit and update an AI action plan by specified deadlines to congressional committees.

Includes provisions for AI leadership, workforce development, partnerships, and risk and bias measures.

Instructs the Director, alongside other officials, to identify regulatory barriers to AI adoption in sectors like healthcare and transportation within one year.

Requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology to report on measures to detect and prevent AI-related security risks and ideological bias, outlining internal reviews, audits, and public disclosures, with criteria and corrective measures used by federal agencies. 

Defines artificial intelligence as specified in the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Official name: HR 5300 Department of State Policy Provisions Act 2025 (Economic Affairs, Study on Geopolitical Strategies and Verification for AI)
Casual name: HR 5300 Department of State Policy Provisions Act 2025 (Economic Affairs, Study on Geopolitical Strategies and Verification for AI)
Short summary: Instructs the Assistant Secretary for Emerging Threats to develop a strategy to maintain U.S. AI leadership, monitor adversaries' AI systems, propose international agreements, and evaluate monitoring mechanisms. Requires a report within two years, with updates on AI developments.
Long summary:
Instructs the Assistant Secretary for Emerging Threats and the Assistant Secretary for Cyberspace and Digital Policy to develop a strategy to maintain U.S. leadership in advanced AI.

Requires this strategy to include methods to monitor AI development by adversaries, proposals for international agreements to limit AI threats, and mechanisms to verify compliance with these agreements.

Assesses evasion strategies by adversaries and proposes countermeasures.

Explores diplomatic options to delay adversaries' AI development and strengthen international cooperation.

Identifies limitations in current strategies and proposes policy recommendations for enhancement, emphasizing diplomatic actions and verification methods requiring further research.

Mandates a report submission two years post-enactment to congressional committees by the Assistant Secretary for Cyberspace and Digital Diplomacy.

Requires updates on significant AI developments impacting U.S. national security.

Defines "covered AI systems" as those posing severe threats, including systems surpassing human experts in high-risk areas or possessing high autonomy.

Official name: Utah House Bill 286 (Artificial Intelligence Transparency Amendments)
Casual name: Utah HB 286 (Artificial Intelligence Transparency Amendments)
Short summary: Enacts the AI Transparency Act, requiring large frontier developers to implement and publish public safety and child protection plans addressing AI-related risks. Mandates reporting of AI safety incidents and prohibits misleading statements about risk management. Establishes whistleblower protections. Effective May 6, 2026.
Long summary:
Enacts the AI Transparency Act to regulate large frontier developers utilizing significant computing for AI model training.

Requires developers to publish detailed public safety and child protection plans, incorporating standards and best practices, to mitigate risks such as catastrophic losses and child safety issues.

Mandates third-party assessments and regular updates to these plans.

Prohibits false statements about risk management and plan compliance, allowing for document redactions to safeguard trade secrets and security.

Establishes reporting mechanisms for safety incidents, requiring prompt disclosure to appropriate agencies and quarterly catastrophe risk assessments.

Protects whistleblowers disclosing potential safety threats, prohibiting retaliatory actions by employers.

Subjects developers to civil penalties for non-compliance, with penalties recoverable through civil action by the Attorney General.

Creates the AI Transparency Enforcement Restricted Account to fund enforcement activities.

Enables employees to seek remedies for wrongful adverse actions related to whistleblowing.

Takes effect May 6, 2026.

Official name: Virginia SB 269 (Mental health service providers)
Casual name: Virginia SB 269 (Mental health service providers)
Short summary: Regulates mental health providers' use of AI for administrative and supplementary support, requiring disclosure and patient consent. Prohibits AI in making therapeutic decisions, direct client interaction, and generating recommendations without approval. Imposes penalties for noncompliance.
Long summary:
Prohibits mental health service providers from using AI systems for independent therapeutic decisions or direct client interactions in therapeutic communication.

Allows AI use for administrative or supplementary support if providers maintain responsibility for related interactions and disclose AI use to clients, who must consent in writing.

Requires providers to ensure AI-generated therapeutic recommendations receive professional review and approval.

Prohibits advertising or offering AI-based therapy without a licensed provider performing services.

Excludes religious counseling, peer support, and public self-help resources from restrictions.

Mandates confidentiality of records and communications per relevant statutes.

Sets a civil penalty up to $10,000 for violations, collected by the Department of Health Professions.

Official name: Unleashing Low-Cost Rural AI Act
Casual name: Unleashing Low-Cost Rural AI Act
Short summary: Designates the Secretary of Energy to commission a National Laboratory study on AI and data center site growth's impact on energy resources, with a focus on infrastructure updates, alternative energy, and impacts on remote areas. Prioritizes expedited compliance with permitting requirements.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Energy to designate a National Laboratory to study the impact of artificial intelligence and data center site growth on U.S. energy supply resources.

Requires the study to determine if infrastructure updates are necessary to support AI and data center co-location.

Assesses alternative energy sources for co-located sites and evaluates impacts on energy costs, supply, and reliability.

Evaluates deficiencies in energy supply resources.

Explores expedited reviews and permitting for AI and data center sites under the National Environmental Policy Act.

Prioritizes studying impacts in remote areas.

Mandates a report submission to relevant Congressional committees within 180 days of the Act's enactment.

Defines key terms including “artificial intelligence,” “co-location,” “National Laboratory,” and “remote area” according to existing legal definitions.

Official name: New York A 6578 (AI Training Data Transparency Act)
Casual name: New York A 6578 (AI Training Data Transparency Act)
Short summary: Requires developers of generative AI models, by January 2027, to publicly document on their websites detailed information about training datasets, including sources, contents, and any modifications. Exempts models for aircraft operation and national security purposes from this requirement.
Long summary:
Enacts the Artificial Intelligence Training Data Transparency Act in New York's general business law.

Requires developers of generative AI models or services available to New Yorkers, from January 2027 onwards, to post data documentation used for AI training on their websites. 

Stipulates that this documentation must include sources and ownership of datasets, purpose-related data descriptions, data point details, and any proprietary or public domain status of datasets.

Mandates disclosure of whether personal, aggregated consumer information, or synthetic data generation was used. 

Exempts models related to national airspace operations or those developed solely for national security, military, or defense purposes, provided they are exclusively for federal entities. 

Defines key terms, including artificial intelligence, developer, generative AI, substantial modification, and synthetic data generation, to clarify responsibilities and expectations under the act.

Requires transparency to foster understanding and trust in AI applications and models.

Official name: HR 5287 China Advanced Technology Monitoring Act 2025 (Annual report on the advanced semiconductor manufacturing capabilities of China)
Casual name: HR 5287 China Advanced Technology Monitoring Act 2025
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Defense to annually report on China's semiconductor capabilities, including AI chipmaking and international collaborations, and assess U.S. export controls' effectiveness, with policy recommendations. Requires publication of unclassified details.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit an annual report on China's semiconductor manufacturing capabilities starting by May 1, 2026, for five years.

Includes key findings and policy recommendations for countering China's advancements in semiconductor manufacturing.

Assesses China's domestic capabilities and industrial policies affecting semiconductors.

Analyzes China's technological advancements in semiconductor and AI chipmaking.

Describes China's international engagements, including partnerships and foreign investments in semiconductor manufacturing.

Evaluates the impact and effectiveness of U.S. export controls and their ability to curb China's semiconductor development.

Assesses implications of Chinese dominance in semiconductors on U.S. competitiveness, security, and economy.

Submits the report in unclassified form with a classified annex, available on a government website and noted in the Federal Register.

Official name: Safeguarding Adolescents From Exploitative BOTs Act
Casual name: SAFE BOTs Act
Short summary: Requires chatbot providers to disclose their systems as AI, not licensed professionals, and provide crisis resources to minors. Prohibits misleading claims about professional licensure. Obligates policy establishment to mitigate harmful content. Mandates Federal Trade Commission enforcement of these provisions.
Long summary:
Requires chatbot providers to clearly disclose to minor users that the chatbot is an artificial intelligence system and provide resources for suicide prevention when prompted.

Prohibits chatbots from falsely claiming to be licensed professionals.

Instructs providers to create policies ensuring chatbots advise breaks after three hours of continuous use and address harmful content related to minors, such as sexual material, gambling, and illegal substances.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance and treat violations as unfair or deceptive practices.

Allows state attorneys general to take legal action if their residents are harmed by violations.

Mandates a study by the Secretary of Health and Human Services on the mental health impacts of chatbots on minors, with a report due in four years.

Prohibits states from enacting laws contradicting these federal provisions.

Clarifies definitions relevant to AI and chatbots, including distinctions for minors and harmful materials.

Official name: Utah H.B. 286 Artificial Intelligence Transparency Amendments
Casual name: Utah H.B. 286 Artificial Intelligence Transparency Amendments
Short summary: Requires large frontier developers in Utah to publish public safety and child protection plans, detailing risk assessments and mitigation strategies. Prohibits misleading statements about risk management. Mandates safety incident reporting and establishes penalties for non-compliance. Creates whistleblower protections.
Long summary:
Enacts the "AI Transparency Act" in Utah, establishing governance over artificial intelligence systems regarding transparency, catastrophic risk, and child protection.

Requires large frontier developers—entities using significant computing power to create AI models—to create, implement, and publish public safety and child protection plans on their websites. These plans must detail assessment methods for catastrophic and child safety risks and involve third-party evaluations.

Mandates developers to report safety incidents and modifications to public safety plans to the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy.

Prohibits false statements regarding risk management and allows redactions to traded-sensitive documents.

Imposes civil penalties for violations, directs penalties to an enforcement account, and protects whistleblowers under specific conditions.

Creates reporting mechanisms and establishes potential civil penalties for non-compliance.

Commences this legislation on May 6, 2026.

Official name: HR 6275 China AI Power Report Act 2025 (A report annually on the advanced artificial intelligence capabilities of China)
Casual name: HR 6275 China AI Power Report Act 2025
Short summary: Require the Secretary of Commerce to annually report on China's AI capabilities, assessing semiconductor production, AI models, regulatory frameworks, and technology diffusion. Prioritize advanced AI system supply chains and recommend measures to strengthen U.S. export controls.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Commerce to annually report on China's advanced AI capabilities, assessing integrated circuits, semiconductor fabrication facilities, and AI models relevant to U.S. national security.

Requires evaluations of Chinese semiconductor manufacturing and electronic design automation companies, focusing on production volumes, technological specifications, and market shares.

Assesses China's public AI funding, research advancements, and adherence to global standards.

Analyzes the impact and effectiveness of U.S. export controls on AI technologies.

Prioritizes the examination of critical semiconductor components and AI systems posing strategic U.S. implications.

Mandates the report to be unclassified with potential classified annexes and comparisons with U.S. capabilities. 

Consults expert entities for thorough analysis.

Official name: HR 7273 NASA Reauthorization Act of 2026 (Title V—Aeronautics)
Casual name: HR 7273 NASA Reauthorization Act 2026 (Title V—Aeronautics)
Short summary: Directs the Administrator to collaborate on unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility research, including UTM and autonomous capabilities. Requires periodic briefings to Congress on progress. Prohibits procurement from certain foreign entities with possible exceptions for national interest.
Long summary:
Regulates the research and development of unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and advanced air mobility, highlighting the importance of collaborations with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and other stakeholders.

Defines advanced air mobility, urban and regional air mobility, and unmanned aircraft and systems.

Requires NASA to conduct research on UTM (unmanned aircraft system traffic management) and autonomous capabilities.

Mandates collaboration with relevant federal agencies, academia, and industry on autonomous aviation to ensure U.S. competitiveness.

Prohibits NASA from procuring UAS from covered foreign entities unless a waiver is issued for national interests and specific purposes.

Establishes the importance of leveraging research for enhancing emergency response operations and promoting information sharing and interoperability in aerial responses to disasters like wildfires.

Encourages hypersonics research coordination between NASA, the FAA, and the Department of Defense to sustain U.S. leadership in high-speed aeronautical advancements.

Official name: Washington HB 2157 (Regulating high-risk artificial intelligence system development, deployment, and use.)
Casual name: Washington HB 2157 (Regulating high-risk AI)
Short summary: Regulates high-risk AI systems, requiring developers to disclose risks and provide documentation. Obligates deployers to implement risk management and complete impact assessments. Establishes consumer protections against algorithmic discrimination and mandates transparency in consequential decisions. Effective January 1, 2027.
Long summary:
Regulates the development and deployment of high-risk AI systems in Washington state.

Defines "high-risk AI systems" as those autonomously making consequential decisions impacting areas like employment, housing, and legal services.

Requires developers to ensure AI systems are free from algorithmic discrimination and mandates compliance with risk management frameworks.

Obligates developers to provide documentation on intended uses, risks, and mitigation strategies of high-risk AI systems.

Mandates deployers to implement risk management programs and conduct impact assessments before deploying high-risk AI systems.

Stipulates disclosure to consumers when interacting with high-risk AI systems, including the purpose and nature of consequential decisions.

Exempts systems used exclusively for research or those complying with federal standards from certain obligations.

Allows civil action against developers/deployers for violations, offering remedies like injunctions and attorneys' fees.

Sets the act’s effective date as January 1, 2027.

Official name: S 3275 Humanoid Robotics Oversight and Blocking of Obtainment from Totalitarians Act of 2025
Casual name: S 3275 Humanoid ROBOT Act of 2025
Short summary: Prohibits executive agencies from contracting humanoid robots from entities in countries of concern. Requires investment reviews by CFIUS for humanoid robot technologies. Directs the Secretary of Defense to report on national security threats posed by humanoid robots.
Long summary:
Title: Humanoid Robotics Oversight and Blocking of Obtainment from Totalitarians Act of 2025

Prohibits heads of executive agencies from entering into or renewing contracts to procure humanoid robots from entities associated with countries of concern.

Prohibits contractors from using humanoid robots from covered entities to support contracts with executive agencies.

Allows the Secretary of Defense to waive these prohibitions for national security or research purposes.

Directs the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council to amend regulations within 180 days to enforce these prohibitions.

Amends the Defense Production Act to require Committee on Foreign Investment review of investments in U.S. businesses producing humanoid robots by entities from countries of concern.

Mandates a report by the Secretary of Defense on national security threats posed by humanoid robots from countries of concern, including analyses and recommendations for improving export controls and addressing privacy and data security risks.

Official name: Healthcare Education in AI Literacy Act
Casual name: HEAL-AI Act
Short summary: Amends the Public Health Service Act to create a grant program, administered by the Health Resources and Services Administration, funding AI education for medical students, residents, and faculty. Requires grantees to report on AI educational integration and outcomes. Prioritizes underserved communities.
Long summary:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to create a grant program administered by the Health Resources and Services Administration.

Establishes funding for the education and training of medical students, residents, and faculty in AI deployment within the medical profession.

Defines AI as machine-based systems generating medical predictions, recommendations, or decisions using both machine and human inputs.

Allocates grants to qualified medical schools and residency institutions, capped at $100,000 annually.

Requires grant-funded programs to address AI diagnostics, treatment recommendations, ethical implications, and practical demonstrations.

Mandates compliance with annual reporting on program objectives, expenditure, and outcomes.

Prioritizes grants for institutions serving medically underserved communities and ensures geographic diversity in grant distribution.

Prohibits grant funds for predatory publishing and limits administrative cost use.

Facilitates collaboration with academic, nonprofit, and government entities.

Requires publicly available educational materials developed with grant funding.

Authorizes $1,000,000 funding annually from 2026 through 2030.

Official name: Texas HB 149 (Relating to regulation of the use of artificial intelligence systems in this state; providing civil penalties.)
Casual name: Texas HB 149 (Regulating AI systems)
Short summary: Establishes the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act to regulate AI systems. Prohibits certain manipulative behaviors and uses of biometric data by AI systems. Requires consumer disclosure when interacting with AI. Creates the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council for oversight and recommendations. Establishes a regulatory sandbox program for innovative AI systems. Enforces compliance through the Attorney General.
Long summary:
Establishes the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act regulating AI use.

Prohibits AI systems from manipulating behavior or performing social scoring by government entities.

Requires clear disclosure to consumers when interacting with AI systems, especially in healthcare.

Restricts government from using AI for biometric identification without consent, protecting constitutional rights.

Prohibits AI development or deployment intending unlawful discrimination or infringing rights.

Sets penalties for violating AI regulations, enforced by the attorney general.

Creates an AI regulatory sandbox for testing AI systems without full regulatory compliance.

Establishes the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council to ensure ethical AI use, suggest reforms, and guide public agencies.

Mandates state agency reports on AI system evaluations for cybersecurity and efficiency.

Grants the attorney general authority to investigate AI system complaints, allowing corrective opportunities.

Designates January 1, 2026, for Act implementation.

Official name: Colorado HB25B-1009 (Artificial Intelligence Systems 2025)
Casual name: Colorado HB25B-1009 (Artificial Intelligence Systems 2025)
Short summary: Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems, starting August 1, 2027, to prevent algorithmic discrimination, perform impact assessments, and disclose risks.
