Outlines specific data documentation requirements, including dataset sources, descriptions, data points, copyright status, and whether synthetic data were used.

Exempts developers documenting data for AI systems solely for security, defense, aircraft operation, or systems under the federal food, drug, and cosmetic act.

Sets compliance expectations to adhere to the current state of the art, including guidance from national standards, without compromising trade secrets.

Designates violations of these requirements as unfair or deceptive acts under Washington's consumer protection act.

Does not apply these requirements if subject to existing federal mandates. 

Establishes provisions as a new chapter in Title 19 RCW.

Official name: California SB-300 (Companion chatbots).
Casual name: California SB-300 (Companion chatbots).
Short summary: Amends regulations for companion chatbots, requiring operators to notify users of AI nature, prevent harmful content, publish safety protocols, and ensure disclosures and break reminders for minors while restricting sexually explicit material in interactions with minors.
Long summary:
Amends the Business and Professions Code to require operators to notify users when interacting with companion chatbots that are artificially generated.

Requires operators to maintain protocols to prevent chatbots from producing content related to suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm, including notifications referring users to crisis service providers.

Obligates operators to publish details of these protocols on their websites.

Instructs operators to notify minors interacting with chatbots that the interaction is with artificial intelligence.

Directs operators to provide reminders to minors every three hours to take breaks and disclose that the chatbot is artificially generated.

Requires operators to prevent chatbots from producing or facilitating sexually explicit material or suggestions for minors.

Official name: Arizona HB 2311 (Artificial Intelligence Service, Disclosures, Requirements 2026)
Casual name: Arizona HB 2311 (Artificial Intelligence Service, Disclosures, Requirements 2026)
Short summary: Regulates operators of conversational AI services to notify minors of AI interactions, prevent sexual content, and provide privacy tools. Requires disclosure of AI nature to prevent users from believing it's human. Imposes penalties for violations, enforceable by the Attorney General. Effective September 30, 2027.
Long summary:
Enacts requirements for operators of conversational AI services, defined as AI programs simulating human conversation, to protect minors.

Requires operators to disclose interactions with AI to minor account holders, either persistently or at regular intervals.

Prohibits operators from incentivizing increased participation of minors through unpredictable rewards.

Obliges operators to prevent AI from producing sexual content or engaging in conversations that could mislead minors to believe interactions are with a human.

Mandates tools for privacy management for minors and, if relevant, their guardians, particularly when account holders are under 13.

Imposes protocols for responding to suicidal ideations by directing users to crisis services.

Prohibits operators from suggesting that AI services provide mental health care.

Imposes civil penalties for violations, enforced by the Attorney General, without establishing a private right of action.

Clarifies that AI model developers are not liable for third-party operator violations.

Official name: Texas SB 815 (Use of AI systems in Utilization Reviews 2025)
Casual name: Texas SB 815 (Use of AI systems in Utilization Reviews 2025)
Short summary: Prohibits a utilization review agent from using automated decision systems for making adverse determinations in health benefit claims. Allows the commissioner to audit these systems. Permits their use for administrative support or fraud detection. Effective January 1, 2026.
Long summary:
Amends the Texas Insurance Code to define "artificial intelligence system" and "automated decision system."

Prohibits a utilization review agent from using an automated decision system to make, wholly or partly, adverse determinations regarding health care services.

Allows the commissioner to audit and inspect a utilization review agent's use of an automated decision system.

Permits the use of algorithms and AI systems for administrative support or fraud detection.

Requires notices of adverse determinations to include reasons, clinical basis, screening criteria, and appeal procedures.

Applies these provisions to health benefit plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.

Sets the Act's effective date as September 1, 2025.

Official name: Colorado HB 25B-1008 (Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence Interactions 2025)
Casual name: Colorado HB 25B-1008 (Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence Interactions 2025)
Short summary: Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems, from October 1, 2026, to prevent algorithmic discrimination, disclose risks and modifications, provide necessary documentation, and undergo annual impact assessments. Obligates disclosure to consumers when interacting with AI. Grants the attorney general oversight authority.
Long summary:
Requires developers of high-risk AI systems in Colorado, from October 1, 2026, to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination and document compliance using model or dataset cards.

Instructs developers to disclose risks of algorithmic discrimination to the attorney general and known deployers, no later than ninety days after discovery.

Mandates deployers of high-risk AI systems to implement risk management programs and conduct annual impact assessments.

Obligates deployers to notify the attorney general if algorithmic discrimination is found within ninety days and disclose relevant policies upon request.

Ensures consumers, interacting with AI systems, are informed that they are engaging with AI.

Empowers the attorney general to review and evaluate compliance through required disclosures, keeping proprietary and privileged information confidential under the Colorado Open Records Act. 

Clarifies that the act takes effect upon specific conditions related to a potential referendum.

Official name: HR 5932 Claims Legitimacy and Evaluation Accountability Nationwide for VA Act 2025 (Utilizing AI for VA Disability rating schedule)
Casual name: HR 5932 CLEAN VA Act 2025
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to implement AI and data analytics to detect irregularities in disability claims. Requires human review of AI findings. Ensures respect for due process and privacy protections. Coordinates oversight with Inspector General and GAO.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to develop and implement a program using data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) systems to identify irregularities or high-risk indicators in disability claims. 

Requires consultation with the Inspector General and the Comptroller General to ensure the program's effectiveness and protect due process and privacy rights.

Models AI systems after existing federal waste and fraud detection systems. 

Requires human review and validation of AI findings before any decisions.

Mandates the Secretary to report on AI integration and propose updates for disability claim processes. 

Requires coordination with the Office of Inspector General and the Government Accountability Office to evaluate tools, identify risks of misidentification, and recommend best practices.

Mandates ethical training for employees to prevent fraud, supervised by the Inspector General. 

Requires reports on its implementation and outcomes to relevant Congressional Committees.

Official name: Illinois HB 3773 (Limit Predictive Analytics Use 2023)
Casual name: Illinois HB 3773 (Limit Predictive Analytics Use 2023)
Short summary: Defines "artificial intelligence" and "generative artificial intelligence." Prohibits employers from using AI for employment decisions that result in discrimination based on protected classes. Requires employers to notify employees about AI use. Directs the Department to implement rules.
Long summary:
Defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system generating outputs like predictions and decisions, influencing environments, including generative AI that mimics human content.

Prohibits employers from using AI in ways that result in discrimination based on protected classes or using zip codes as proxies for these classes.

Requires employers to inform employees about the use of AI in recruitment, hiring, promotion, and other employment aspects.

Instructs the Department to develop rules for implementing and enforcing these AI-related provisions, including requirements for employer notice to employees, such as timing and method. 

Sets the effective date for these regulations on January 1, 2026.

Official name: S 3374 Secure and Feasible Exports of Chips Act of 2025
Casual name: S 3374 SAFE Chips Act of 2025
Short summary: Prohibits the issuance of licenses for export, reexport, or in-country transfer of advanced integrated circuits to foreign adversaries. Requires denial of such license applications. Excludes circuits not designed for data centers. Defines 'advanced integrated circuit' with specific technical parameters.
Long summary:
Amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to prohibit issuing licenses for exporting, reexporting, or transferring advanced integrated circuits to foreign adversaries.

Requires the Secretary to deny applications for such licenses specifically to countries or entities headquartered in foreign adversary countries.

Excludes advanced integrated circuits not designed or marketed for data centers from this prohibition.

Defines 'advanced integrated circuit' based on specific technical parameters, including processing performance and bandwidth metrics.

Allows the Secretary to update these technical parameters with majority approval from the End-User Review Committee, and requires briefing Congressional committees prior to these updates.

Specifies that 'foreign adversary country' includes certain United States Code countries and regions like Macau and Hong Kong.

Mandates assessment of how modifications affect China's AI capabilities and U.S. computing advantage.

Official name: Montana HJ 4 (Interim study of artificial intelligence)
Casual name: Montana HJ 4 (Interim study of AI)
Short summary: Requests the Legislative Council to study AI laws, develop a code of ethics, assess transparency and liability, and evaluate AI's benefits and risks in Montana. Requires findings presented by September 15, 2026, to the 70th Legislature.
Long summary:
Requests the Legislative Council to assign a committee or staff to study artificial intelligence regulation and ethics in Montana.

Instructs the examination of current laws and regulations from Montana, other states, and the federal government concerning AI.

Directs research on a code of ethics for AI and a bill of rights for citizens.

Requires examination of transparency, disclosure, and liability issues for AI entities.

Assesses AI's benefits and risks to Montana's agencies and residents, focusing on employment, rights, privacy, and economic welfare.

Specifies completion by September 15, 2026, with findings reported to the 70th Legislature.

Official name: New Jersey A 4732 (Notification Requirements for Artificial Intelligence Companion Models 2026)
Casual name: New Jersey A 4732 (Notification Requirements for AI Companion Models 2026)
Short summary: Requires operators of AI companions to notify users that they are not communicating with a human at the start and every three hours during interactions. Imposes a $15,000 civil penalty per violation. Defines AI companion and operator terms.
Long summary:
Defines "AI companion" as a system using generative AI to simulate human-like relationships through personalized interactions, unsolicited questions, and ongoing personal dialogue.

Requires operators to notify users clearly and conspicuously at the start of every AI companion interaction, and at least every three hours, that they are not communicating with a human.

Specifies that the notification can be verbal or written.

Imposes a civil penalty of $15,000 per violation on operators who fail to comply with the notification requirements.

Authorizes the Superior Court and municipal court to enforce penalties according to the "Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999."

Takes effect immediately upon enactment.

Official name: HR 5300 Department of State Policy Provisions Act 2025 (International Security Affairs, Study on Geopolitical Strategies and Verification for AI)
Casual name: HR 5300 Department of State Policy Provisions Act 2025 (International Security Affairs, Study on Geopolitical Strategies and Verification for AI)
Short summary: Instructs the Assistant Secretary for Emerging Threats to develop a strategy to maintain U.S. leadership in AI, including monitoring foreign AI systems, proposing international agreements, identifying verification methods, assessing evasion tactics, and examining diplomatic strategies. Requires reporting to Congress.
Long summary:
Assigns the Assistant Secretary for Emerging Threats, in coordination with the Assistant Secretary for Cyberspace and Digital Policy, to develop a strategy to maintain U.S. leadership in advanced AI.

Requires the strategy to include methods for monitoring AI developments by foreign adversaries, agreements to limit AI deployments, verification mechanisms, and countermeasures against evasion techniques.

Calls for examining diplomatic and geopolitical options if the U.S. delays adversaries’ AI developments and addresses limitations in AI strategies.

Obligates submission of a report detailing the strategy to Congress two years post-enactment.

Mandates timely updates to Congress during this period on significant AI developments affecting U.S. national security.

Defines "covered AI systems" as advanced AI systems posing severe national security threats if misused by adversaries, particularly those surpassing human capabilities or operating autonomously.

Official name: New York S 8420 (Relates to requiring advertisements to disclose the use of a synthetic performer)
Casual name: New York S8420 (Disclosure of Synthetic Performers)
Short summary: Requires advertisers with actual knowledge to disclose the use of synthetic performers created using generative AI in advertisements. Imposes penalties for non-compliance. Excludes expressive works and certain audio-only or language translation uses from these requirements.
Long summary:
Amends the general business law to require disclosures in advertisements featuring synthetic performers.

Defines "artificial intelligence," "generative artificial intelligence," and "synthetic performer."

Requires any person creating an advertisement for commercial purposes to disclose conspicuously the inclusion of a synthetic performer if there is actual knowledge of such use.

Imposes a civil penalty of $1,000 for the first violation and $5,000 for subsequent violations.

Exempts advertisements for expressive works, such as motion pictures and television programs, when the use of synthetic performers is consistent with their use in the work.

Excludes audio advertisements and those involving AI use for language translation of a human performer from these requirements.

Clarifies the act does not affect rights under specified civil rights laws or protections under 47 U.S.C. § 230 related to interactive computer services.

Specifies the act takes effect 180 days after becoming law.

Official name: North Carolina EO (Advancing Trustworthy AI That Benefits All North Carolinians)
Casual name: North Carolina EO (Advancing Trustworthy AI That Benefits All North Carolinians)
Short summary: Establishes the North Carolina AI Leadership Council to advise on AI strategy and policy. Creates the AI Accelerator for AI governance, research, and training. Requires Cabinet agencies to propose AI use cases. Develops statewide AI literacy and fraud prevention training program.
Long summary:
Establishes the North Carolina AI Leadership Council to advise and support AI strategy, policy, and training, advancing the state’s AI literacy and governance.

Requires the Council to create a State AI Strategic Roadmap and recommend policies on AI ethics, safety, transparency, and collaboration across sectors.

Sets the Council's annual reporting duties to include progress on AI initiatives and challenges.

Creates the North Carolina AI Accelerator within the Department of Information Technology for centralized AI governance and promotion of responsible AI use.

Mandates state agencies to propose AI use cases for Accelerator review, prioritizing piloting and implementation.

Instructs the development of AI literacy and fraud-prevention training programs accessible to the general public.

Sets the expiration of this order on December 31, 2028, unless extended or rescinded by the Governor. 

The Accelerator may continue operations following the order's expiration.

Official name: HR 5272 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
Casual name: HR 5272 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
Short summary: Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to prohibit the distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated media affecting Federal candidates or elections with intent to influence or solicit funds. Allows civil actions for violations and exempts certain media entities.
Long summary:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to prohibit knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media of candidates in federal elections with the intent to influence elections or solicit funds.

Defines “materially deceptive AI-generated media” as content created using AI/machine learning that misleads about a person’s appearance, speech, or conduct.

Excludes from prohibition media broadcast by news entities if acknowledged as potentially inauthentic, and satire or parody.

Allows affected candidates to seek injunctive relief or damages if deceptive media is distributed.

Entitles successful plaintiffs to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs.

Clarifies a violation as defamation per se for related legal actions.

Maintains severability, ensuring the rest of the Act remains unaffected if a provision is found invalid.

Official name: National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
Casual name: National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
Short summary: Specifies safety requirements for GenAI services, including training data safety, model safety, and safety measures. Instructs service providers to ensure data source safety, intellectual property protection, personal information protection, and model output safety. Requires monitoring, user transparency, and complaint mechanisms. Outlines responsibilities for annotators and service providers concerning model performance, data annotation, and user data usage.
Long summary:
Specifies comprehensive safety requirements for generative AI (GenAI) services, focusing on training data safety, model safety, and safety measures.

Requires service providers to assess and filter data sources to exclude illegal content, manage intellectual property, and protect personal information.

Demands safety training and assessment for annotators, with distinct roles for data annotation tasks.

Mandates technical measures to ensure model content accuracy, reliability, and regulatory compliance.

Instructs service providers to implement continuous monitoring, emergency management measures, and secure model updates.

Requires transparency about service applications, limitations, and user data handling.

Obligates user choice concerning their data usage and establishes transparent complaint mechanisms.

Demands service stability and continuity through backup and recovery strategies.

Sets additional requirements for on-device model services, including security policy updates and vulnerability remediation. 

Aims to align safety practices with legal standards, promoting responsible GenAI service deployment.

Official name: S 1213 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
Casual name: S 1213 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
Short summary: Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to prohibit knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media to influence elections or solicit funds. Exempts bona fide news, satire, and parody. Allows impacted individuals to seek injunctive relief and damages.
Long summary:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media in Federal election activities.

Defines 'deceptive AI-generated media' as media altered by AI to seem authentic, misleading a reasonable person.

Exempts media presented in honest newscasts, or as satire, and mandates acknowledgments of questionable authenticity in broadcasts.

Allows covered individuals, whose voices or likenesses appear in such deceptive media, to seek injunctive relief or damages against violators.

Entitles legal actions under these provisions to precedence following Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

Permits courts to grant attorney's fees and costs to prevailing parties.

Places the burden of proof on plaintiffs to show violations with clear and convincing evidence.

Includes a severability clause ensuring the Act's remainder remains in effect if any provision is invalidated.

Official name: HR 6361 Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act 2025
Casual name: HR 6361 Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act 2025
Short summary: Prohibits the Secretary of Health and Human Services from implementing the WISeR model. Prohibits testing any new Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation models that use AI for prior authorization under traditional Medicare.
Long summary:
Prohibits the Secretary of Health and Human Services from implementing the WISeR model, which aims to reduce wasteful and inappropriate services using prior authorization in Medicare.

Amends Section 1115A(b)(2) of the Social Security Act to restrict testing of future Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation models that implement prior authorization, including those utilizing artificial intelligence, under traditional Medicare.

Limits the Secretary's testing authority by ensuring that no new models providing for prior authorization, either independently or through AI, can be selected for items or services reimbursable under Medicare parts A and B.

Official name: S.4046 - Economy of the Future Commission Act of 2026
Casual name: Economy of the Future Commission Act of 2026
Short summary: Establishes the Economy of the Future Commission to develop legislative recommendations addressing economic changes from AI adoption. Tasks include evaluating AI's impact on workforce, education, and safety, and proposing standards, industry partnerships, and research strategies. Requires interim and final reports.
Long summary:
Establishes the Economy of the Future Commission to develop legislative recommendations addressing economic changes from artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.

Requires the Commission to evaluate impacts of AI on workforce development, education, social safety nets, and government standards.

Prescribes the creation of strategies for AI research investment and partnerships, and addresses AI in autonomous vehicles, energy needs, and AI-enabled robotics.

Instructs the Commission to prepare interim and final reports on AI's economic impacts, including employment and revenue forecasts.

Specifies the composition of the Commission, including ten congressional appointees and multiple non-voting Deputy Secretaries.

Authorizes the Commission to conduct hearings, issue subpoenas, and secure information from federal agencies.

Exempts the Commission from the Federal Advisory Committee Act and the Freedom of Information Act.

Provides a budget of $5,250,000 and specifies the termination of the Commission 120 days after the final report’s submission.

Official name: 2026 IT-17 Use of Artificial Intelligence in State of Ohio Solutions
Casual name: Ohio 2026 Administrative Policy 17 (Use of AI in State of Ohio Solutions)
Short summary: Requires Ohio state agencies to ensure AI solution governance encompasses ethical considerations, security, and privacy. Instructs the AI Council to oversee generative AI implementations, manage data governance, and provide training. Mandates public disclosure of AI use and human verification of AI decisions.
Long summary:
Establishes statewide requirements for AI use, including planning, implementation, procurement, security, privacy, and governance.

Applies to all Ohio state agencies and requires AI use to align with AI Council-approved solutions.

Mandates agencies to define, document, and review AI use cases, test data quality, and ensure human oversight of AI outputs.

Instructs agencies to provide workforce training on AI use and ethical considerations in coordination with the Ohio Department of Administrative Services.

Sets procurement guidelines for AI solutions, including review of AI systems for security and privacy compliance and demands supplier disclosure of Generative AI use.

Requires AI systems to implement security controls, ensure compliance with privacy laws, and guard against adversarial threats.

Designates the Chief Data Officer Council to manage data governance for AI systems and mandates AI Council oversight on AI adoption impacts and framework establishment.

Official name: President Trump’s Cyber Strategy for America
Casual name: President Trump’s Cyber Strategy for America 2026
Short summary: Promotes AI security by securing the AI technology stack, implementing AI-enabled cyber tools, adopting agentic AI for defense, and ensuring global stability through cyber diplomacy. Encourages innovation in AI security and frustrates foreign platforms that censor and surveil.
Long summary:
Targets the use of AI to secure and modernize federal networks, adopting AI-powered cybersecurity solutions and emphasizing agentic AI for secure network defense and disruption.

Promotes AI security by securing the AI technology stack and ensuring innovation advances global stability.

Encourages AI innovation in ways that protect privacy and deter adversaries.

Calls for swift implementation of AI-enabled cyber tools to detect and divert threats.

Promotes talent and capacity building by innovating education and training for the cyber workforce, fostering public-private partnerships.

Advocates for streamlining regulations to enhance AI and cybersecurity agility.

Defines responsibilities for federal and private entities to ensure AI and digital technology development aligns with security and innovation goals.

Emphasizes the role of AI in promoting U.S. interests and countering foreign AI platforms that impose censorship and surveillance.

Official name: HR 6306 AI Fraud Deterrence Act 2025 (AI for the commission of financial crimes)
Casual name: HR 6306 AI Fraud Deterrence Act 2025
Short summary: Increases mail, wire, bank fraud, and money laundering penalties when committed with AI assistance. Defines AI as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020. Prohibits AI impersonation of federal officials, excluding protected satire and parody.
Long summary:
Increases penalties for financial crimes involving artificial intelligence (AI), such as mail, wire, and bank fraud, by amending relevant sections of title 18, United States Code. 

Raises fines for mail and wire fraud committed with AI to up to $1,000,000 and imprisonment to 20 years. 

Sets fines for bank fraud with AI involvement at up to $2,000,000 and imprisonment for 30 years. 

Defines AI as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020. 

Increases penalties for money laundering involving AI, including fines up to $1,000,000 or thrice the transaction value and imprisonment for 20 years.

Amends impersonation of federal officials using AI, imposing fines up to $1,000,000 and imprisonment of 3 years. 

Clarifies permissible uses of AI in satire or parody if clearly disclosed as non-authentic.

Official name: New York S 1169 (New York AI Act)
Casual name: New York S 1169 (NY AI Act)
Short summary: Establishes obligations for AI developers and deployers to ensure AI systems do not cause harm, focusing on preventing algorithmic discrimination. Prohibits social scoring AI systems. Requires audits, reporting, and risk management for high-risk AI systems. Outlines remedies for violations.
Long summary:
The New York Artificial Intelligence Act establishes regulations for AI systems to protect civil rights and encourage safe AI innovation. 

Prohibits algorithmic discrimination by requiring developers and deployers of AI to prevent biases that disadvantage people based on protected characteristics.

Obligates covered developers and deployers to conduct audits on high-risk AI systems, ensuring transparency and accountability, with the guidance of independent auditors.

Enforces the prohibition on social scoring AI systems that lead to unjustified differential treatment or violate fundamental rights.

Requires developers and deployers to implement risk management policies, reporting requirements, and appeal processes for consequential AI-driven decisions.

Grants the Attorney General authority to enforce compliance, issue injunctions, and impose penalties for violations.

Establishes whistleblower protections preventing retaliation against employees who disclose violations related to AI systems.

Takes effect one year after becoming law, with specific provisions enforced after a two-year period.

Official name: HR 6530 AI Training for National Security Act 2025 (Training on AI cybersecurity for the Armed Forces and the Department of Defense)
Casual name: HR 6530 AI Training for National Security Act 2025
Short summary: Requires the Department of Defense's Chief Information Officer to revise annual cybersecurity training for Armed Forces members and civilian employees, including content on unique AI-related cybersecurity challenges, within one year of the Act's enactment.
Long summary:
Require the Secretary of Defense, via the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, to update mandatory annual cybersecurity training.

Include content related to unique cybersecurity challenges posed by artificial intelligence in the training.

Apply this updated training to both members of the Armed Forces and civilian employees of the Department of Defense.

Set a deadline for these revisions to be made within one year of the Act's enactment.

Official name: HR 6591 Computer Science for All Act of 2025 (Increase access to PreK-12 computer science education)
Casual name: HR 6591 Computer Science for All Act 2025
Short summary: Authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants for computer science education expansion, including artificial intelligence. Require recipients to prepare students for AI technologies. Mandate reporting on grant use and program impact with disaggregated data.
Long summary:
Authorizes the Secretary of Education to award grants for expanding access to computer science education from prekindergarten through grade 12.

Requires eligible entities, such as states, local educational agencies, and Tribal schools, to ensure high school students have access to computer science education within five years of receiving grants.

Directs grantees to use funds for teacher training, expanding learning materials, and supporting underrepresented students, with possible inclusion of AI in classrooms.

Permits the formation of consortia or partnerships for grant applications.

Limits equipment purchase costs to a maximum of 15% of grant funds.

Mandates reporting by grantees on student reach, disaggregated by demographics.

Obligates the Secretary to report to Congress after five years, with recommendations for program expansion.

Establishes funding authorization of $250 million annually over five years.

Amends existing legislation to incorporate computer science education data tracking and competencies.

Official name: HR 6573 AI Talent Act 2025 (Establish Federal agency technology and artificial intelligence talent teams to improve competitive service hiring)
Casual name: HR 6573 AI Talent Act 2025
Short summary: Establishes agency technology and AI talent teams for hiring support, improves AI hiring practices, and develops technical assessments. Directs the Office of Personnel Management to create a Federal AI talent team for pooled hiring, training, and platform development.
Long summary:
Establishes Federal agency technology and AI talent teams to enhance competitive service hiring practices for AI positions.

Allows agencies to form talent teams, including roles such as recruiters and subject matter experts, to support AI governance and innovation.

Tasks these teams with improving examinations, writing job announcements, sharing certificates of eligibles, and facilitating hiring.

Permits the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to establish a Federal technology and AI talent team to support pooled hiring and create technology platforms.

Authorizes OPM to ensure agencies use best practices, develop technical assessments, and share resources for AI hiring.

Enables the creation and customization of technical assessments for competitive service positions, shared across examining agencies.

Requires OPM to host an online platform for sharing and customizing assessments.

Defines terms related to agencies, examinations, examining agencies, subject matter experts, and technical assessments.

Official name: A bill to establish Federal agency technology and artificial intelligence talent teams to improve competitive service hiring practices, and for other purposes.
Casual name: S3410 AI Talent Team Act (2025-2026)
Short summary: Establishes federal agency technology and AI talent teams to enhance AI governance, innovation, and hiring practices. Empowers the Office of Personnel Management to support cross-government AI hiring, develop assessments, and create platforms for sharing assessments. Encourages existing platforms use for technical assessments.
Long summary:
Establishes federal agency technology and AI talent teams to enhance hiring practices for AI-related positions.

Authorizes agencies to form talent teams consisting of shared certificate coordinators, recruiters, and assessment experts to manage AI governance and risk.

Requires agency talent teams to improve examinations, craft job announcements, share certificates of eligibles, and facilitate competitive service hiring.

Allows the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to create a Federal technology and AI talent team for pooled hiring actions, training, and technology platform development.

Permits OPM to expand its hiring experience team to focus on AI-related roles.

Directs individuals with relevant expertise to collaborate with human resources for developing and administering technical assessments.

Enables the sharing and customization of assessments among agencies via an online platform managed by OPM.

Requires agencies to use existing hiring platforms like USA Hire for conducting assessments, where practical.

Official name: Responsible and Ethical AI Labeling Act
Casual name: REAL Act
Short summary: Requires Federal officials to disclose content created or manipulated using generative AI with clear disclaimers. Assigns the Office of Management and Budget to establish compliance regulations. Enforces audits, reporting, and corrective actions for non-compliance. Defines relevant terms.
Long summary:
Requires Federal officials to disclose if they publish content created or manipulated using generative artificial intelligence (AI) by including a disclaimer.

Specifies the disclaimer must clearly state the content's AI origin and provide a brief explanation of how it was generated or altered.

Exempts non-public communications, classified content with retained summaries, and minor visual alterations from the disclosure requirement.

Directs the Office of Management and Budget Director to issue regulations for compliance within 180 days.

Mandates annual compliance audits by the President, Vice President, and agency heads, with results published on public websites.

Requires retraction and corrective communication for any content published in violation.

Obliges timely corrective action plans for non-compliance, with potential disciplinary action for federal employees and contractors.

Defines key terms like "generative artificial intelligence" and applies the Act 90 days post-enactment.

Official name: Drone Safety Enhancement Act
Casual name: Drone Safety Enhancement Act
Short summary: Instructs NASA to collaborate with the FAA and others on research into unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility. Requires NASA to brief Congress on research progress within 18 months. Definitions provided for relevant aviation terms, including advanced air mobility.
Long summary:
Facilitates collaboration between NASA and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), along with other agencies, academia, and industry, to conduct research on unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility, including UTM and autonomous capabilities.

Requires the Administrator of NASA, within 18 months of enactment, to brief the appropriate congressional committees on research progress.

Defines key terms, including "advanced air mobility," which encompasses both urban and regional air mobility using advanced, potentially autonomous aircraft technologies.

Clarifies that "appropriate committees of Congress" refers to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

Establishes that "UTM" refers to an unmanned aircraft system traffic management system or service.

Official name: GUARD Act of 2025
Casual name: S3454 GUARD Act
Short summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to establish National Security and Defense AI Institutes at eligible institutions. Provides financial assistance for research, testbeds, and workforce development in AI. Requires competitive review and limits funding to U.S.-based institutions.
Long summary:
Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to establish National Security and Defense Artificial Intelligence Institutes at eligible host institutions.

Requires these Institutes to focus on AI research for national security, establish partnerships with diverse organizations, create innovation ecosystems, and support interdisciplinary research and workforce development.

Permits the Secretary to award financial assistance to establish these Institutes, to be used for data management, testbeds for AI systems, educational activities, access to computing resources, technical support, and other activities.

Mandates a competitive, merit-based process for awarding financial assistance and collaboration with other federal departments.

Specifies that financial assistance is only available to U.S.-based entities with a five-year award term, renewable once.

Defines eligible host institutions as U.S. higher education institutions or senior military colleges conducting Department of Defense-sponsored research.

Official name: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
Casual name: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
Short summary: Prohibits impersonation scams using AI, enforced by the FTC. Requires disclosures for AI use in telemarketing. Establishes an AI Scams Advisory Group. Directs the FTC to report AI scams and update its web portal. Modifies communications regulations.
Long summary:
Enacts the "Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act" to combat AI-enabled fraud.

Prohibits impersonation scams using AI, such as replicating voices or images to defraud.

Designates the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce these prohibitions as unfair or deceptive practices.

Amends the Telemarketing and Consumer Fraud and Abuse Prevention Act to include text messages and video conferencing, requiring disclosure if AI is used to simulate human interaction.

Updates the Communications Act of 1934 to broaden definitions related to AI and require disclosure at the beginning of communications using AI.

Instructs the FTC to update its web portal with information on AI-enabled scams and establish consumer complaint procedures.

Establishes an AI Scams Advisory Group consisting of various federal, state, and industry representatives to develop educational materials and best practices.

Requires the FTC to submit annual reports to Congress on AI-enabled scams, their types, and policy recommendations to prevent them.

Official name: S 3555 Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025
Casual name: S 3555 Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act 2025
Short summary: Imposes sanctions on certain foreign persons related to China. Prohibits U.S. investments in specific national security-related technologies, including AI, in countries of concern. Requires U.S. persons to notify covered transactions. Mandates Treasury to enforce regulations and provide reports.
Long summary:
Enacts the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, emphasizing prohibitions and notifications regarding investments in countries of concern, notably China.

Requires the U.S. Treasury Secretary and Commerce Secretary to regulate and possibly prohibit U.S. investments in foreign persons involved with technologies deemed harmful to national security, including artificial intelligence systems and related sectors.

Directs the President to impose sanctions on identified ‘covered foreign persons’ and requires annual reporting to Congress about such individuals and enforcement actions.

Encourages multilateral engagement with allies to develop comparable mechanisms preventing the development of technologies by countries of concern.

Defines critical terms such as ‘covered foreign person’ and ‘prohibited technology,’ identifying crucial sectors like AI that may have impacts on military, intelligence, and surveillance capabilities.

Establishes a process for creating and maintaining a public database of entities involved in prohibited technologies.

Official name: HR 6848 Detecting and Evaluating Foreign Exploitation of Novel Drones Act 2025
Casual name: HR 6848 DEFEND Act 2025
Short summary: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct an annual assessment of terrorism threats from the use of unmanned aircraft systems by foreign adversaries. Evaluates operational risks, including AI usage, and terrorist methodologies.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit an annual assessment of terrorism threats related to the proliferation and malicious use of unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) by foreign adversaries and terrorist organizations.

Requires the assessment to analyze methods, trends, and technologies used for surveillance, disruption, and attacks on critical infrastructure, as well as intelligence and data exploitation.

Evaluates risks of UAS attacks on U.S. security, vulnerabilities, and infrastructure, including potential for chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear delivery.

Demands the inclusion of emerging technologies like AI, autonomous systems, and swarm tactics to enhance UAS effectiveness.

Involves collaboration with the private sector and other federal agencies for comprehensive threat analysis and countermeasure development.

Mandates the creation of training modules for law enforcement to counter UAS threats.

Requires the submission of these reports to Congress in both classified and unclassified forms.

Official name: HR 6875 Artificial Intelligence Oversight of Verified Exports and Restrictions on Weaponizable Advanced Technology to Covered High-Risk Actors Act 2025
Casual name: HR 6875 AI OVERWATCH Act 2025
Short summary: Requires the Under Secretary of Commerce to license exports of specific integrated circuits to certain countries. Prohibits general licenses. Involves Congress in certifications prior to approval. Exempts trusted U.S. persons from some requirements. Demands a national security strategy.
Long summary:
Requires the Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security to obtain a license for the export, reexport, or in-country transfer of certain integrated circuits, specifically to entities in countries of concern, such as China and Russia.

Prohibits general licensing and mandates prior certification to Congress, ensuring exports do not enhance military or intelligence capabilities of those countries.

Exempts "trusted United States persons" from certain license requirements if they maintain ownership and control.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce, alongside other federal officials, to submit a national security strategy addressing the implications of integrated circuit exports to countries of concern.

Terminates previously issued licenses for exports to entities in countries of concern and imposes a temporary prohibition on new licenses until a national security strategy is submitted to Congress.

Official name: S 3586 AI for Mainstreet Act 2026 (Require small business development centers to assist small business with the use of AI)
Casual name: S 3586 AI for Mainstreet Act 2026
Short summary: Amends the Small Business Act to require small business development centers to assist small businesses in evaluating AI. Provides guidance on AI use for operations, such as cybersecurity and data protection. Defines "artificial intelligence" per existing legislation.
Long summary:
Amends the Small Business Act to require small business development centers to assist small businesses with artificial intelligence use.

Directs these centers to offer information, guidance, and training on AI, covering best practices, operational integration, data protection, cybersecurity improvement, regulatory compliance facilitation, and customer trust enhancement.

Instructs centers to conduct outreach to small businesses regarding AI use to the extent practical.

Defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Specifies that no additional funds are authorized for implementing these provisions.

Official name: H.R. 6996 (Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act 2026)
Casual name: H.R. 6996 (Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act 2026)
Short summary: Establishes U.S. policy to maintain AI dominance, promote U.S. AI technology globally, and counter Chinese influence. Instructs the Secretary of Commerce to facilitate AI exports and develop security measures. Initiates studies and reports on AI export success and global deployment impacts.
Long summary:
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to establish a program for industry consortia to export the U.S. full AI stack to allies, ensuring adherence to U.S.-approved security standards.

Instructs the Secretary of State to eliminate foreign barriers to exporting the U.S. full AI stack, including through diplomatic strategies and industry engagement.

Directs a study by the Secretary of State, in coordination with other officials, on the global deployment impacts of the U.S. full AI stack.

Tasks the Secretary of Commerce with developing security measures for U.S. AI semiconductor products to prevent unauthorized foreign access.

Requires creation of an "AI Full Stack Confidence Initiative" to assure foreign purchasers of the U.S. AI stack's security and efficacy.

Mandates biannual reporting of the "AI export success tracker," detailing U.S. AI stack deployment globally.

Designates responsibilities across various governmental entities to maintain U.S. dominance and secure U.S. AI technologies against foreign threats.

Official name: HR 7058 Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act 2026
Casual name: HR 7058 Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act 2026
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of State to assess risks from foreign adversaries using generative AI maliciously. Instructs annual reporting on AI-based threats, including synthetic media, cyber operations, and weapons development. Recommends ways to mitigate these AI-related national security risks.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of State, in consultation with relevant federal agencies, to assess annually the risks posed by foreign adversaries using generative AI for malicious activities, beginning 180 days after the Act's enactment.

Mandates that these assessments include analyses of incidents involving malicious AI usage for propaganda, military capabilities, cyber operations, and more, as well as emerging trends and implications for U.S. foreign policy.

Directs the submission of the assessments, including unclassified and potentially classified portions, to appropriate congressional committees and posting the unclassified sections publicly.

Instructs the Department of State to engage diplomatically to address foreign adversaries' use of generative AI, promote responsible AI use in international settings, and mitigate threats to U.S. national security.

Official name: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
Casual name: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
Short summary: Require covered agencies to establish civil rights offices focused on AI-related bias and discrimination. Mandate reporting on algorithmic harms every two years. Instruct the DOJ Civil Rights Division to form an interagency working group on AI and civil rights.
Long summary:
Requires each covered agency that uses, funds, or regulates algorithms to establish an office of civil rights focused on bias, discrimination, and other harms associated with algorithms.

Tasks these offices with employing experts to address issues related to algorithmic impacts on protected characteristics.

Instructs these offices to submit biennial reports to congressional committees, detailing their findings on algorithm-related biases and discrimination, actions taken to mitigate these harms, stakeholder engagement, and legislative recommendations.

Directs the Assistant Attorney General in charge of the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice to form an interagency working group focused on covered algorithms and civil rights.

Allocates necessary funding to covered agencies to implement the Act’s provisions.

Official name: Children Harmed by AI Technology Act
Casual name: CHAT Act
Short summary: Requires companion AI chatbots to implement age verification measures, affiliate minor accounts with verified parental accounts, and block minors from sexually explicit content. Mandates monitoring for suicidal ideation, and obligates FTC enforcement. Establishes a safe harbor for compliance.
Long summary:
Requires companion AI chatbots to implement user account creation and robust age verification processes for all users, freezing existing accounts until verified.

Classifies users as minors or adults and mandates parental account affiliation and parental consent for minors.

Obligates covered entities to block minors' access to sexually explicit chatbots and monitor for suicidal ideation, providing appropriate resources where needed.

Requires notifications to users that they are interacting with AI, not humans.

Instructs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to issue compliance guidance and treats violations as unfair or deceptive practices under FTC Act enforcement.

Allows state attorneys general to pursue civil actions against violators, with certain procedural requirements.

Grants covered entities safe harbor if they demonstrate good faith in age verification and alignment with the FTC's guidance or industry standards.

Designates the FTC as the primary enforcement authority and preserves its jurisdiction.

Official name: S 3742 AV Safety Data Act 2026 (Improve incident reporting with respect to certain autonomous vehicles)
Casual name: S 3742 AV Safety Data Act 2026
Short summary: Requires the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to mandate monthly incident reports from autonomous vehicle operators detailing unplanned stoppages and collisions. Directs the administrator to publish these reports online. Limits data collection to non-personal information when Level 2 systems are engaged.
Long summary:
Enacts the "AV Safety Data Act" to enhance incident reporting for certain autonomous vehicles.

Requires the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) to establish regulations within 90 days mandating that manufacturers and operators of vehicles with Automated Driving Systems or Level 2 Advanced Driver Assistance Systems submit incident reports.

Obligates covered entities to provide monthly reports on vehicle miles traveled, collision incidents causing injury to vulnerable road users or others, and details of unplanned stoppage events.

Permits data reporting only if the Level 2 system was engaged or during specified conditions, without including drivers' personally identifiable information.

Instructs the Administrator to make submitted reports publicly available online in a machine-readable format 120 days post-enactment.

Allows the Administrator to rescind or adjust these regulations after ten years to modify the required reporting frequency and scope.

Official name: HR 7294 AI for Secure Networks Act 2026
Casual name: HR 7294 AI for Secure Networks Act 2026
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Commerce to study AI's impacts on telecommunications security, including its improvement uses and risks. Requires collaboration with the FCC and industry stakeholders, and mandates a report to Congress with potential legislative recommendations.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Commerce to conduct a study on the impacts of artificial intelligence on telecommunications network security.

Requires the study to analyze AI's role in improving network features such as threat detection, resiliency, energy efficiency, and security integrations with Open Radio Access Network and virtualized security technology.

Examines potential risks AI may pose to network security.

Mandates consultation with the Federal Communications Commission and industry stakeholders for research and development insights.

Obligates submission of a report within one year to specific congressional committees, potentially including legislative recommendations.

Provides an opportunity for public comment on the report before submission.

Official name: HR 7323 Defense Technology Hubs Act of 2025 (Regional hubs for development of defense-related technologies)
Casual name: HR 7323 Defense Technology Hubs Act 2026
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish regional defense technology hubs, focusing on AI and emerging technologies. Authorizes grants, ensures strict cybersecurity measures, and mandates annual progress reports. Aligns with existing defense innovation efforts like DARPA and DIU.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to establish the Defense Technology Hubs Program to advance defense technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Designates regional hubs to foster innovation in emerging technologies with military applications.

Solicits applications from eligible consortia to form these hubs, assessing their capabilities in areas such as AI, autonomy, and edge computing.

Awards grants to hubs for technological development and transition projects.

Ensures compliance with cybersecurity standards and export regulations, preventing unauthorized access and foreign participation.

Develops intellectual property guidelines balancing national security and commercial interests.

Administers the program through the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering.

Coordinates with existing initiatives like DARPA to avoid duplication.

Requires annual progress reports and independent evaluations of program effectiveness.

Allocates $375 million for fiscal years 2026-2030 to support the program, with $75 million specifically for grants.

Official name: Copyright Labeling and Ethical AI Reporting Act
Casual name: CLEAR Act
Short summary: Requires individuals using copyrighted works in generative AI models to notify the Register of Copyrights. Enforces civil penalties for non-compliance. Directs the Register to create a public database of notices and issue filing regulations.
Long summary:
Requires individuals using copyrighted works to train generative AI models to submit a notice to the Register of Copyrights, detailing each copyrighted work and providing a URL for publicly available training datasets.

Establishes a 30-day notice filing timeframe prior to commercial use or release of a generative AI model.

Instructs the Register to issue regulations for notice procedures within 180 days of the Act's effective date.

Allows copyright owners to sue if proper notice is not submitted, imposing civil penalties of at least $5,000 per violation, with a cap of $2,500,000 annually per violator. 

Permits courts to award attorney’s fees and issue injunctions stopping the use of the work until notice compliance.

Directs the Register to maintain a publicly accessible online database of all submitted notices.

Official name: S 933 NASA Transition Authorization Act 2025, Title V—Aeronautics
Casual name: S 933 NASA Transition Authorization Act 2025, Title V—Aeronautics
Short summary: Define advanced air mobility and urban air mobility in terms of AI's role in aircraft technologies. Require NASA to collaborate on unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility research, alongside other federal agencies, industry, and academia.
Long summary:
Define "advanced air mobility" (AAM) as transportation using manned or unmanned aircraft for urban and regional mobility, incorporating advanced technologies.

Require the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Administrator to continue hypersonic research with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and Department of Defense (DoD), updating the hypersonic research roadmap in consultation with industry and academia.

Instruct the NASA Administrator to report on unmanned aircraft systems and AAM research, coordinating with the FAA, other agencies, academia, and industry.

Authorize NASA to research Advanced Capabilities for Emergency Response Operations, especially for improving aerial wildfire responses.

Permit NASA to conduct research on hydrogen aviation technologies, contingent on available appropriations.

Emphasize collaboration with academic institutions for cutting-edge research, leveraging expertise to address aeronautical challenges, and inspire STEM careers.

Official name: Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Inclusion Act
Casual name: Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Inclusion Act
Short summary: Directs the National Science Foundation to provide awards for developing AI literacy programs, prioritizing marginalized communities. Requires federal agencies to report on integrating AI literacy into workforce, business, and education strategies. Instructs public availability of agency reports and consultations with stakeholders.
Long summary:
Directs the Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) to make awards for AI literacy programs to eligible entities, focusing on local communities learning from trusted sources.

Permits use of funds for developing educational materials, providing training to marginalized communities, and evaluating program effectiveness.

Encourages prioritization for programs serving marginalized communities and with a demonstrated record in technology education.

Requires award recipients to report annually on program descriptions, demographics served, and program impacts.

Mandates reports to Congress from the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce, and Education, and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration, detailing how AI literacy can advance workforce development, business competitiveness, education, and national security.

Requires public availability of reports and interagency consultation with stakeholders.

Defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence literacy" as understanding AI basics and societal effects.

Official name: TEST AI Act of 2025
Casual name: TEST AI Act of 2025
Short summary: Requires the Director of NIST to establish a pilot program with testbeds for AI measurement standards. Involves collaboration with the Secretary of Energy and a working group. Develops standards for AI reliability, performance, security, and privacy.
Long summary:
Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish a pilot program using testbeds to develop measurement standards for evaluating AI systems used by Federal agencies.

Instructs the Director to coordinate with the Secretary of Energy and consult with a newly established Artificial Intelligence Testing Working Group.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of Energy to enter a memorandum of understanding to facilitate coordination and resource sharing.

Establishes a Working Group to advise on developing measurement standards, comprising representatives from government, the private sector, and academia, but excludes citizens of covered foreign countries.

Requires the Working Group to develop a strategy identifying necessary measurement standards and methods for reliable, secure, and unbiased AI systems.

Instructs the Director to develop testbeds within two years and allows hiring experts for guidance.

Mandates a report to Congress on findings and recommendations for improving and continuing testbed and standards development.

Official name: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
Casual name: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
Short summary: Prohibits Federal contractors from using DeepSeek by High Flyer unless waived for national security by the Secretary of Commerce. Requires the Secretary of Commerce to report on AI threats from countries of concern, detailing risks and recommending actions.
Long summary:
Prohibits federal contractors with active contracts from using the DeepSeek application or any service by High Flyer for contract fulfillment, unless waived by the Secretary of Commerce in consultation with the Secretary of Defense for national security or research purposes.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to submit a report within one year detailing national security threats from AI platforms based in or affiliated with countries of concern.

Includes analysis of censorship laws, propaganda use, export control circumvention, and privacy/data security threats related to AI applications.

Includes recommendations for administrative and legislative measures to protect U.S. data security and privacy.

Permits the report to be in unclassified form with a possible classified annex.

Official name: HR 3303 America—Israel AI Cooperation Act 2025 (Exception to export  license requirements for certain advanced integrated circuits to Israel)
Casual name: HR 3303 America—Israel AI Cooperation Act 2025
Short summary: Require the Secretary of Commerce to amend the AI Diffusion framework. Include Israel in the amendment list for exporting advanced integrated circuits, granting it the same export exceptions and requirements as other included countries.
Long summary:
Title "America--Israel AI Cooperation Act" requires the Secretary of Commerce to modify the "Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion" rule.

Includes Israel among countries specified in Supplement No. 5 to part 740 of title 15, Code of Federal Regulations, for advanced integrated circuit exports.

Ensures exports to Israel of such AI-related items are subject to the same requirements and exceptions as those to the other listed countries.

Instructs the Undersecretary of Commerce for Industry and Security to execute these modifications.

Official name: Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2025
Casual name: Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2025
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Defense to ensure competition, security, and data rights in AI, cloud, and data infrastructure procurement. Directs updates for safeguarding government data. Requires annual reports on AI market competition from the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to promote security, resiliency, and competition in AI, cloud, and data infrastructure procurement through a competitive award process, maintaining exclusive government rights to data, and prioritizing multi-cloud technology where feasible.

Directs the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office to ensure government data is protected and not used without authorization for commercial AI product improvement.

Subjects violations of these data protections to penalties, including fines and contract termination, with the possibility of exemptions for national security.

Mandates annual reporting by the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, on AI competition, barriers to entry, and market power concentrations, including exemption details and recommendations for legislative or administrative actions.

Ensures public access to the report through the Department of Defense's website and other means.

Official name: AI Whistleblower Protection Act
Casual name: HR3460 AI Whistleblower Protection Act
Short summary: Prohibits employers from retaliating against AI whistleblowers reporting security vulnerabilities or violations. Enables affected individuals to file complaints with the Secretary of Labor or pursue legal action. Ensures protection of rights and remedies for these whistleblowers.
Long summary:
Prohibits employers from retaliating against individuals who report AI security vulnerabilities or AI violations.

Defines "AI security vulnerability" and "AI violation" to include failures to ensure the safety and legality of AI systems.

Covers employees and independent contractors, protecting them when they provide information to authorities, participate in investigations, or report issues internally.

Permits aggrieved individuals to file complaints with the Secretary of Labor or pursue legal action in district court if the complaint is not resolved within 180 days.

Grants prevailing whistleblowers remedies including reinstatement, double back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees.

Establishes a statute of limitations for filing actions, with a maximum of 10 years.

Prohibits waivers or alterations of these rights and remedies through any contractual agreements or employment conditions, including arbitration clauses.

Official name: FRAUD Act of 2025
Casual name: FRAUD Act of 2025
Short summary: Amends title 38 to require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to use an IT system with machine learning and analytics to detect fraud, waste, and abuse in Veterans Health Administration programs, ensuring integration with existing systems and annual reporting to Congress.
Long summary:
Amends title 38 to require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to use an information technology system to detect fraud, waste, and abuse in the Veterans Health Administration's programs.

Utilizes processes and systems to analyze and reanalyze claims submitted by healthcare entities under Veterans Community Care Program for potential fraud.

Includes continuous monitoring, data analysis, analytic models, and post-payment checks in the IT system to identify and predict fraudulent claims.

Ensures integration with existing claims processing systems, log storage, analysis, machine learning to reduce false positives, and updates to detect new fraud models.

Directs use of funds from the Department of Veterans Affairs franchise fund to implement these systems.

Requires the Secretary to report annually on the system's effectiveness, savings achieved, and system enhancement plans to Congressional Veterans' Affairs Committees.

Mandates implementation within one year of enactment.

Official name: Leadership in Critical and Emerging Technologies Act
Casual name: Leadership in CET Act
Short summary: Establishes a pilot program to expedite U.S. patent applications for AI and other emerging technologies. Requires the Director of the USPTO to oversee and provide public information on the program, ensuring applications meet certain criteria and consulting with federal agencies as needed.
Long summary:
Establishes a pilot program by the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office to expedite patent applications for technologies, including those with AI capabilities such as machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI systems.

Requires the program to encourage U.S. leadership in emerging technologies by providing prompt examination for these patents.

Permits the Director to set conditions for participating in the program and to consult with federal agencies like the Attorney General and the Secretary of Defense.

Demands that applicants not be foreign entities of concern and limits inventors to five total program applications.

Terminates the program after five years or 15,000 applications, with a possible renewal.

Obligates the Director to report program impact to Congress and make information publicly available online.

Official name: SAFE CROSS Act
Casual name: SAFE CROSS Act
Short summary: Require the Federal Railroad Administration to study AI-enabled sensors at rail crossings for safety. Instruct the publication of study results and best practices online, benefiting governmental and private entities involved in rail crossing safety.
Long summary:
Directs the Administrator of the Federal Railroad Administration to conduct a study on AI-enabled sensors at rail crossings as a safety measure.

Requires the study to review existing pilot programs and deployments of such sensors.

Includes a cost-benefit analysis comparing AI-enabled sensors with other safety measures, such as grade separations.

Identifies best practices for implementing and using AI-enabled sensors at rail crossings.

Instructs the Administrator to publish the study’s results and best practices to a publicly accessible website within 30 days of completion.

Targets the published recommendations for use by federal, state, tribal, and local government entities, as well as private entities responsible for rail crossing safety.

Official name: HR 3375 AI Training Extension Act of 2025 (Amend the Artificial Intelligence Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act to expand AI training)
Casual name: HR 3375 AI Training Extension Act of 2025
Short summary: Amends the Artificial Intelligence Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act to expand AI training to include employees in various executive branch roles. Requires the Administrator, in coordination with OMB, to establish the AI training program, incorporating existing programs and addressing AI capabilities, risks, and best practices.
Long summary:
Amends the Artificial Intelligence Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act to expand AI training within the executive branch.

Defines the roles of employees in acquisition, data, and technology positions, alongside management officials and supervisors, to facilitate this training expansion.

Instructs the Administrator of General Services, in coordination with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to establish the AI training program.

Allows the Administrator to incorporate existing training into the program when relevant.

Requires the training program to cover the capabilities, risks, and benefits of AI, including privacy concerns and data's role in AI development.

Directs the Administrator to incorporate participant feedback into program updates.

Removes the phrase "for the Acquisition Workforce" from the Act's title, broadening its scope.

Official name: Flexible Acquisition of Software Technology Act
Casual name: FAST Act
Short summary: Authorize the Secretary of Defense to procure software and data services to support AI systems. Require issuance of regulations for AI-related procurement oversight. Define AI systems, data service models, and software types to guide these activities.
Long summary:
Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to procure software and data as a service to support artificial intelligence systems.

Permits the procurement of software and data either as a service or as a supply to meet military operational needs.

Allows the modification, research, development, testing, and evaluation of software for AI systems.

Enables the use of appropriated funds for these activities.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to issue or update regulations to govern and oversee software and data procurement for AI systems.

Defines key terms including "Artificial Intelligence System," "Data as a Service," "Data as a Supply," and "Software as a Service" to clarify the delivery models and capabilities involved.

Official name: Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act
Casual name: Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act
Short summary: Establishes a two-year pilot program using predictive risk-scoring algorithms for overseeing Medicare payments, beginning by January 1, 2026. Instructs the Secretary to collaborate with industry, notify beneficiaries, and employ human reviews for suspensions based on algorithm findings.
Long summary:
Establishes a pilot program using predictive risk-scoring algorithms to oversee Medicare payments for durable medical equipment and clinical diagnostic laboratory tests.

Requires the Secretary to implement this program for two years, starting by January 1, 2026.

Limits participation to beneficiaries who opt-in and receive electronic Medicare Summary Notices.

Considers factors such as lack of a prior provider relationship, aberrant billing patterns, and ownership changes to assess transaction risk.

Collaborates with industry representatives for program development.

Adopts a predictive algorithm to score transaction risks and conducts thorough testing before implementation.

Notifies beneficiaries and providers about algorithm use and data handling.

Allows beneficiaries to address or confirm high-risk transactions.

Triggers alerts and follows up on suspended transactions through Medicare Summary Notices.

Permits the termination or re-issuance of Medicare cards to prevent fraud.

Ensures suspensions are based on human review informed by the algorithm.

Official name: Responsible Innovation and Safe Expertise Act of 2025
Casual name: RISE Act of 2025
Short summary: Grants immunity to AI developers from civil liability for errors if specific transparency and documentation standards are met. Requires developers to maintain and update model cards and specifications. Limits immunity from claims involving recklessness, fraud, or non-professional uses.
Long summary:
Establishes conditional immunity from civil liability for AI developers when their systems are used by learned professionals in professional services, provided specific transparency and documentation criteria are met.

Requires developers to publicly release and maintain a model card and model specification before AI deployment, allowing limited redactions for trade secrets with justifications.

Mandates developers to provide documentation detailing AI systems' limitations and appropriate use domains.

Specifies that immunity does not cover acts of recklessness or willful misconduct and excludes claims for fraud or misrepresentation.

Includes a duty for developers to update relevant documentation within 30 days of new AI versions or discovered failure modes.

Expressly preempts state law claims except those based on conduct outside professional use or on fraud and misrepresentation.

Takes effect on December 1, 2025, and applies to acts or omissions from that date onward.

Official name: Tennessee House Bill 2325
Casual name: Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council Act
Short summary: Establishes the Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council to recommend AI action plans for state government, focusing on economic benefits, responsible use, labor market impacts, and transparency. Requires annual reports through 2028, with a final report due by December 31, 2028.
Long summary:
Establishes the Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council to guide AI awareness, education, and usage in state government.

Requires the council to submit an action plan to the governor for leveraging AI to improve government service efficiency and capture economic benefits.

Mandates the council to report annually on AI's impact on the labor market, propose legal and policy changes, and recommend workforce development strategies.

Directs the council to submit a final report by December 31, 2028, outlining AI governance frameworks, risk analyses, and recommendations for AI deployment in government.

Requires all state departments to cooperate with the council and allows the council to consult with AI experts.

Specifies that the council members will not receive compensation but will be reimbursed for travel expenses.

Repeals the act on December 31, 2028, and takes effect upon becoming law.

Official name:
National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1513 ("Physical and cybersecurity procurement requirements for artificial
intelligence systems")
Casual name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1513 ("Physical and cybersecurity procurement requirements for artificial intelligence systems")
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a cybersecurity framework for Department of Defense AI and machine learning technologies. Requires tailoring of security requirements in consideration of costs versus benefits and encourages collaboration with private sector and academia.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a comprehensive framework for cybersecurity and physical security for AI and machine learning systems within the Department of Defense.

Requires this framework to address insider threats, supply chain risks, adversarial tampering, and unintended data exposure.

Specifies that the framework should integrate existing cybersecurity standards, like NIST, and prioritize systems of interest to cyber threat actors.

Instructs the amendment of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to enforce these security practices on contractors.

Mandates cost-benefit analysis concerning security requirements, considering potential development delays against national security benefits.

Encourages collaboration with industry and academia in developing the framework.

Demands an implementation plan with clear timelines, resources, and metrics, and mandates submission of a status report to congressional defense committees within 180 days of the Act's enactment.
