Official name: Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act
Casual name: H.R.2246 Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act
Short summary: Imposes sanctions on Chinese entities involved in defense, surveillance sectors. Prohibits U.S. investments in covered national security transactions and prohibits holding securities of listed Chinese companies. Requires U.S. persons to notify certain investments involving AI-development-related technologies in China.
Long summary:
Imposes sanctions on certain Chinese entities and individuals engaged in defense or surveillance sectors through the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Requires notification for U.S. investments in prohibited technologies and establishes penalties for violations, reflecting stringent oversight on national security transactions involving China.

Mandates divestment of securities by U.S. persons from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List, prohibiting holding after a specified period.

Outlines procedures for approving exceptions to these prohibitions through waivers, subject to congressional notification and review.

Establishes a framework for using collaborative reports and a public database for covered foreign persons while protecting sensitive information.

Outlines regulations and processes to enforce prohibitions, commands an annual report to assess developments, and encourage multilateral cooperation to prevent China’s acquisition of sensitive technologies. 

Designates Commerce and Treasury authorities to oversee implementation and allows Presidential delegation of some powers.

Official name: IRONDOME Act of 2025
Casual name: IRONDOME Act of 2025
Short summary: Accelerates the development of autonomous agents to defend the U.S. homeland and armed forces against cruise missiles and drone raids. Uses all available authorities to ensure a cost-effective approach.
Long summary:
Accelerates the development of autonomous agents to defend against cruise missiles and drones.

Requires the Secretary to use all available authorities to achieve this goal.

Aims to enhance cost-effective defense of the United States homeland and forward-deployed armed forces.

Official name: H.R.1142 - To amend the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines, and for other purposes.
Casual name: H.R.1142 Amending the Public Health Service Act for Drug Adherence Guidelines
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines using artificial intelligence and machine learning, aiming for 90% adherence for Medicare Part B and D drugs. Promotes usage of generic and biosimilar drugs.
Long summary:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to mandate the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines aimed at 90 percent adherence for Medicare part B and D drugs.

Requires incorporation of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in these guidelines.

Promotes, to the greatest extent possible, the use of generic and biosimilar drugs.

Official name: H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
Casual name: H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
Short summary: Establishes responsibilities for promoting resilient supply chains and emerging technologies, including AI, to strengthen U.S. national security. Requires Assistant Secretary to assess and respond to supply chain vulnerabilities. Encourages reduced reliance on certain foreign goods. Forms Supply Chain Resilience Working Group.
Long summary:
Assigns the Assistant Secretary of Commerce new responsibilities to promote the resilience of critical supply chains and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. 

Establishes a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group to assess and address vulnerabilities in critical supply chains and technologies.

Mandates consultations with various stakeholders, including government entities and international allies, to improve supply chain readiness and response to disruptions.

Encourages domestic production and reduced reliance on countries posing national security risks for critical goods and technologies, including AI.

Protects voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information from public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

Requires periodic assessments and strategy reports to Congress on supply chain resiliency and emerging technology impacts.

Sets a 10-year term for the act's provisions and requires a public comment period for certain designations and reports.

Official name: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities
Casual name: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities, § 92.210
Authority: Department of Health and Human Services
Collections: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
Short summary: Prohibits covered entities from discriminating in health programs using patient care decision support tools based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability. Requires identifying and mitigating discrimination risks in these tools.
Long summary:
Prohibits covered entities from discriminating based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability through the use of patient care decision support tools in health programs or activities.

Requires covered entities to make reasonable efforts to identify uses of such tools that employ input variables or factors measuring race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.

Mandates covered entities to make reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risks from identified tools in their health programs or activities.

Official name: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025
Casual name: Leveraging AI to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025
Short summary: Requires annual AI reviews of federal regulations for redundancy and obsolescence. Mandates OMB and NIST consultation to ensure AI system accuracy and security. Compels agencies to review, amend, or rescind regulations deemed outdated or redundant. Implements expedited regulatory changes.
Long summary:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to annually implement a process using artificial intelligence to identify redundant or outdated federal regulations.

Mandates the use of an AI system that meets strict standards for accuracy, transparency, accountability, and national security risk.

Obliges agencies to review identified redundant or outdated regulations within 30 days and make a final determination of their status.

Commands the rescission or amendment of regulations found to be redundant or outdated within 30 days after determination.

Requires the public publication of any determination with a brief explanation, with an option for a classified annex to Congress if necessary.

Amends Title 5 of the United States Code to facilitate the expedited rescission and amendment of redundant or outdated regulations identified through AI review.

Official name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 40001 ("Coast Guard mission readiness")
Casual name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 40001 ("Coast Guard mission readiness")
Short summary: Appropriates $75 million for the Coast Guard to contract, acquire, or procure autonomous maritime systems, enhancing AI and automated capabilities for maritime operations. Specifies funding to improve maritime domain awareness and upgrade technology infrastructure supporting AI-driven systems.
Long summary:
Appropriates $24,593,500,000 to the Coast Guard for fiscal year 2025 to enhance mission readiness, with funds available until September 30, 2029.

Allocates $266,000,000 for long-range unmanned aircraft and related systems, emphasizing security along the maritime border.

Provides $75,000,000 to acquire or contract services for autonomous maritime systems.

Designates $170,000,000 for strengthening maritime domain awareness, including the cyber domain, highlighting technological advancements for improved security.

Specifies $825,000,000 for technological improvements, including command, control, communication, computer, and cyber assets maintenance, which may indirectly involve AI enhancements.

Focuses on substantial funding for upgrading and acquiring various maritime and aerial assets, reflecting indirect implications for AI through potential advanced equipment and systems integration.

Official name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 50404 ("Transformational artificial intelligence models")
Casual name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 50404 ("Transformational artificial intelligence models")
Short summary: Mobilizes National Laboratories to partner with industry for structuring Department of Energy's data for AI and machine learning models. Provides models via American science cloud to aid microelectronics and new energy technologies development.
Long summary:
Demands that the Secretary of Energy mobilize National Laboratories  to partner with industry to curate and preprocess Department of Energy data for artificial intelligence and machine learning models.

Initiates seed efforts to develop self-improving artificial intelligence models for science and engineering using curated data.

Allows curated data to be used for developing next-generation microelectronics.

Provides artificial intelligence models to the scientific community through the American science cloud.

Appropriates $150,000,000, available through September 30, 2026, to fund the outlined initiatives.

Official name: General Purpose AI Code of Practice, Transparency Chapter
Casual name: General Purpose AI Code of Practice, Transparency Chapter
Short summary: Requires general-purpose AI model providers to comply with AI Act obligations, particularly Articles 53 and 55. Obligates providers to maintain, disclose, and update model documentation for compliance assessment. Tasks the AI Office with overseeing adherence to these obligations.
Long summary:
Provides a Code of Practice to enhance compliance with Articles 53 and 55 of the AI Act, focusing on human-centric and trustworthy AI while ensuring protection against AI's harmful effects.

Guides providers of general-purpose AI models in fulfilling documentation obligations per the AI Act, ensuring updated Model Documentation is accessible to the AI Office and downstream providers.

Requires disclosures of contact information to facilitate information requests from the AI Office and downstream providers, ensuring compliance assessment for high-risk AI systems through timely information provision.

Advises on maintaining the quality, security, and integrity of documented information, suggesting adherence to technical standards and protocols.

Encourages voluntary public transparency, allowing public access to non-confidential information, and providing training content summaries as required by AI Act provisions in line with Article 53(1)(d).

Exempts open-source AI models without systemic risk from these requirements, aligning obligations with the proportionality principle.

Official name: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence Regulation in Ukraine: Vision of the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine 2024
Casual name: White Paper on AI Regulation in Ukraine 2024 (Stages 1 and 2)
Short summary: Supports the development of tools to help businesses and the state prepare for future regulation, including a methodology to assess AI's impact on human rights; proposes creating general and sectoral AI recommendations and voluntary codes of conduct; calls for the gradual implementation of EU regulation and the creation of an AI supervisory body before EU accession.
Long summary:
Proposes the development of tools to help businesses and the state prepare for future regulation, including a methodology for assessing AI's impact on human rights and a regulatory sandbox.

Promotes the voluntary labeling of AI systems to foster transparency, trust, and accountability.

Calls for the creation of general and sectoral recommendations, voluntary codes of conduct, and a web portal for the Responsible AI center. 

Explains how the proposed soft tolls and training tools are expected to positively impact businesses, citizens, and the state.

Advocates for drafting Ukrainian AI regulation law immediately after the adoption of EU AI regulation; supports the gradual implementation of EU AI regulation and the deferral of certain provisions in order to provide more preparation time.

Emphasizes the need for Ukraine to transpose EU AI Regulation and establish an AI supervisory body before EU accession.

Encourages partnerships with leading AI platforms to address potential human rights violations; proposes applying the Trusted Flagger concept, which would involve Ukrainian NGOs acting as Trusted Flaggers that monitor and filter complaints about human rights violations related to AI use.

Allows stakeholders, such as government bodies and academia, to provide feedback on the White Paper within 3 months of its publication.

Official name: Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 5051, of 2019
Casual name: Brazil Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 5051, of 2019
Short summary: Requires human supervision in AI systems and assigns civil liability for damages from AI usage to the supervisor.  Requires state entities to train workers on AI and create specific workers' protection policies.
Long summary:
Establishes nonexhaustive principles for AI usage in Brazil rooted in human dignity, transparency, and the protection of privacy and personal data.

Requires AI decision-making systems to be auxiliary to humans, with supervision compatible with the type and severity of decisions.

Attributes civil liability for AI-induced damages to the system’s human supervisor.

Directs government entities to promote AI education in the workforce, create worker protection policies, and ensure gradual AI adoption.

Requires government AI applications to enhance service quality and efficiency for the population.

Effective 45 days after publication.

Official name: Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 2338, of 2023
Casual name: Brazil Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 2338, of 2023
Short summary: Establishes regulations for developing, implementing, and using AI systems in Brazil, emphasizing human rights, privacy, non-discrimination, and transparency. Requires risk assessment for AI applications, prohibiting excessive-risk systems. Defines governance and accountability for high-risk AI, stipulating rights to contest automated decisions. Designates a competent authority for oversight and enforcement, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance. Encourages innovation through regulatory sandboxes while ensuring data protection and ethical AI usage.
Long summary:
Sets general rules for AI development, implementation, and use in Brazil, prioritizing human rights, democratic values, and innovation.

Establishes principles such as transparency, non-discrimination, and human oversight for AI systems.

Defines 'artificial intelligence system' and 'artificial intelligence agents,' and assigns regulation and oversight to a designated competent authority.

Mandates that AI systems undergo preliminary risk assessment, with high-risk systems requiring algorithmic impact assessments.

Prohibits AI systems that exploit vulnerabilities or use subliminal techniques to harm individuals.

Requires transparency and accountability in AI systems, including the right to contest automated decisions and request human intervention.

Stipulates civil liability provisions, holding AI providers or operators accountable for damages, with stricter liability for high-risk systems.

Encourages innovation through regulatory sandboxes and considers AI impact on copyright and intellectual property.

Designates a competent authority for enforcement, inspection, and issuance of sanctions for non-compliance.

Official name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 225 ("Advanced robotic automation for munitions manufacturing")
Casual name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 225 ("Advanced robotic automation for munitions manufacturing")
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of the Army to support robotic automation in munitions manufacturing. Includes objectives like safe system design, increased production, cyber security, and workforce training. Coordinates with relevant departments and briefs Congress by March 1, 2026.
Long summary:
Require the Secretary of the Army to implement a program to enhance robotic automation in munitions manufacturing at government-owned, contractor-operated facilities.

Include objectives such as designing safe, scalable robotic systems for munitions production, increasing production capacity, developing secure cyber infrastructure for integrating factory operations, and supporting workforce training in robotics and advanced manufacturing.

Coordinate with the Joint Program Executive Office Armaments and Ammunition and other relevant Army components during program execution.

Require a briefing to congressional defense committees by March 1, 2026, detailing program progress, lessons learned, and recommendations for broader adoption of robotic automation technologies in the defense sector.

Official name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 245 ("Biological data for artificial intelligence")
Casual name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 245 ("Biological data for artificial intelligence")
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop requirements ensuring DoD-funded biological data resources facilitate AI use. Defines "qualified biological data," includes metrics for data quality, cybersecurity safeguards, privacy protections, and allows national security exceptions. Requires the Secretary to consult relevant sectors about the feasibility of new requirements and review existing frameworks.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement requirements for storing biological data from Department of Defense-funded research to facilitate the use of such data for advanced computational methods, including AI, within one year of the act's enactment.

Defines "qualified biological data resource" using criteria such as data type, dataset size, federal funding amount, data sensitivity, and other factors deemed appropriate by the Secretary of Defense.

Imposes tiered cybersecurity safeguards and access controls for data storage.

Establishes exceptions for national security and requirements for individual privacy protection.

Consults with military and research officials, as well as private and academic stakeholders, to prevent overly burdensome requirements.

Incorporates existing federal frameworks and standards as appropriate.

Official name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1512 ("Artificial intelligence and machine learning security in the Department of Defense")
Casual name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1512 ("Artificial intelligence and machine learning security in the Department of Defense")
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a cybersecurity policy for AI/ML systems no later than 180 days after the act is passed.  Develop a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of the AI/ML policies. Addresses potential security risks, implements methods to mitigate those risks, and establishes standard policy.  Requires a comprehensive report of the threats and cybersecurity measures by August 31, 2026.
Long summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a cybersecurity policy for AI/ML systems no later than 180 days after the act is passed.  

Addresses potential security risks specific to AI, such as model serialization attacks, model tampering, data leakage, adversarial prompt injection, model extraction, model jailbreaks, and supply chain attacks.

Implements methods to mitigate those risks using industry-recognized frameworks to ensure AI/ML systems are trustworthy.

Requires training for the workforce of the Department of Defense to ensure personnel are prepared to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities that are specific to AI/ML.

Establishes standard policy for governance, testing, and auditing of AI systems.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a comprehensive review and report of the effectiveness of the AI/ML cybersecurity practices, including an identification of gaps in the existing security measures, by August 31, 2026.

Official name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 350 ("Pilot program for data-enabled ground vehicle maintenance")
Casual name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 350 ("Pilot program for data-enabled ground vehicle maintenance")
Short summary: Establishes a pilot program for the Armed Forces to apply AI in ground vehicle maintenance. Requires assessment of AI feasibility, effectiveness, cost savings, and cybersecurity risks. Requires a report to Congress. Terminates authority by January 1, 2029.
Long summary:
Establishes a pilot program using commercially available AI technologies to improve ground vehicle maintenance in the Army, Navy, or Air Force.

Requires the Secretary concerned, in consultation with the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, to implement the program within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Directs the Secretary to assess the feasibility, effectiveness, and cost savings of AI-driven maintenance, and to identify cybersecurity and integration challenges.

Requires a report to Congress on the pilot program's activities within one year of enactment.

Terminates the pilot program on January 1, 2029.

Official name: SAFE from PRC Investments Act
Casual name: SAFE from PRC Investments Act
Short summary: Amends the Securities Exchange Act to require public companies and exchange-traded funds to disclose ties to the Chinese government or Communist Party, including board memberships, financial operations, military involvements, and data management, focusing on governance and security implications.
Long summary:
Requires public companies and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) investing in companies with ties to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to disclose whether senior officials of the PRC government or Communist Party of China (CPC) sit on their boards or have executive roles.

Mandates disclosure of cash held in PRC operations, restrictions on cash repatriation, and details of assets, liabilities, and technology transfers.

Obligates reporting on interactions with CPC officials, expenditures on PRC operations, and any lobbying activities in the United States.

Compels ETFs to reveal ownership, CPC branches, contractual agreements, and involvement in PRC industrial policies or military contracts of invested PRC companies.

Requires disclosure of PRC companies’ products and services, U.S. defense contracts, and involvement in sectors like AI, telecommunications, and semiconductors.

Official name: New Jersey S 2723
Casual name: New Jersey S 2723 ("Integrated Digital Experience Act")
Short summary: Authorizes the Chief Technology Officer to evaluate AI, machine learning, and cloud services use by state agencies for public services. Requires agencies to submit IT modernization plans leveraging data analytics and enhancing digital services, ensuring mobile-friendly and accessible websites.
Long summary:
Requires each state agency to develop and submit an information technology modernization and improvement plan to the Chief Technology Officer within one year of request.

Mandates the plan to include strategies for improving digital services using data analytics, cloud computing, electronic forms, and digitized workflows, ensuring mobile-friendly and accessible websites.

Authorizes the Chief Technology Officer to review these plans in collaboration with the Chief Innovation Officer.

Mandates the Chief Technology Officer to annually evaluate the feasibility of using AI, machine learning, and cloud services for public services, and to develop data analytics capabilities for policy development.

Requires the development of metrics to assess each agency's implementation of a modern digital experience, updated at least every two years and reevaluated every three years.

Official name: Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023
Casual name: CAMPUS Act
Short summary: Prohibits Department of Defense funding to entities contracting with Chinese institutions supporting the People's Liberation Army. Denies visas to individuals from these institutions. Limits educational funding and strengthens U.S.-Taiwan partnerships for Mandarin instruction. Lowers foreign gift disclosure threshold.
Long summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to create and annually update a list of China-based universities that support the People’s Liberation Army, with the first submission to Congress due within 180 days of enactment.

Requires the Department of Defense to restrict research, development, testing, and evaluation funding from being provided to U.S. entities that maintain contracts with institutions on that list or on the Commerce Department’s Entity List.

Rars entities from being cleared to host or store classified information unless they certify they have no active research partnerships with listed institutions.

Prohibits federal K-12 education funding from going to schools that maintain contracts with China-domiciled entities.

Authorizes grants to U.S. schools to support Mandarin language instruction and Chinese cultural programming in partnership with Taiwan.

Prohibits federal research funds for entities contracting with listed Chinese entities.

Lowers the reporting threshold for foreign gifts to institutions of higher education from $250,000 to $50,000.

Official name: PAID Act, Sec. 3 (Requirements for Private Passenger Automobile Insurers)
Casual name: PAID Act, Sec. 3 (Requirements for Private Passenger Automobile Insurers)
Short summary: Prohibits insurers from using specific personal factors, including gender and credit score, to determine car insurance rates. Requires submission to FTC to ensure no disparate impacts from algorithms. Mandates public access to underwriting rules.
Long summary:
Recognize that auto insurance is required in all states except New Hampshire, and that driving uninsured can lead to serious penalties.

Recognize that many insurers use variables to determine what consumers pay based on individual details (income proxies), not actual crash risk, which can block customers from preferred rates.

Prohibit auto insurers from using certain personal factors to decide whether a consumer can get coverage or what a consumer pays.

Prohibit insurers from considering gender, education level, job or occupation, employment status, homeownership status, ZIP code, census tract, marital status, credit score, consumer reports, previous insurer, or prior purchase of insurance from that insurer when determining eligibility or price.

Require insurers to submit information to the FTC within one year of enactment and every two years thereafter.

Require insurers to provide the FTC information showing that their marketing, underwriting, pricing, claims handling, fraud investigations, and any algorithms or models used in these activities do not create a disparate impact.

Require insurers to make underwriting rules and rate filings available for public inspection.

Clarify what counts as a violation and prohibit any use of banned factors that raises costs, restricts coverage, or blocks discounts.

Preserve the authority of federal and state agencies to enforce prohibitions against unfair or deceptive practices.

Recognize that state regulations still apply and that federal law overrides state law only to the extent a state rule conflicts with this Act.

Official name: Alabama SB 78
Casual name: Alabama SB 78 ("Council on Advanced Technology")
Short summary: Establishes the Alabama Council on Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence to review and advise on AI use and development. Requires annual reports with recommendations. Comprises appointed experts and legislative members. Emphasizes diversity in appointments. Effective one year after approval.
Long summary:
Establishes the Alabama Council on Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence.

Requires the council to review and advise the Governor and Legislature on the use and development of advanced technology and artificial intelligence.

Composes the council of 22 members, including appointees from the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Speaker of the House, and Senate President Pro Tempore, and the Secretaries of Commerce and Information Technology, or their designees.

Mandates that non-legislative appointees have expertise in AI, technology, ethics, privacy, workforce development, or computer science.

Stipulates that the council meets at least twice a year and allows virtual participation.

Obliges the council to submit an annual report with policy recommendations on AI and advanced technology to the Governor and Legislature.

Enforces diversity in appointments regarding gender, race, and geography.

Prohibits salary for non-legislative members but allows expense reimbursement; provides legislative members with regular compensation for meeting attendance.

Sets the act’s effective date to one year post-approval.

Official name: REGULATION (EU) 2024/1689 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending Regulations (EC) No 300/2008, (EU) No 167/2013, (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2019/2144 and Directives 2014/90/EU, (EU) 2016/797 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
Casual name: EU AI Act
Short summary: Implements a risk-based regulatory framework for AI, with specific attention to single-purpose AI systems used in risky contexts and general-purpose AI systems with significant capability. Imposes risk-dependent requirements related to accuracy, cybersecurity, evaluation, monitoring, transparency, and registration. Defines exceptions, penalties, and governance structures.
Long summary:
Classifies AI systems into unacceptable, high, limited, and minimal risk categories, defining specific regulatory requirements for each category. Requires strict monitoring and quality management for high-risk systems. 

Establishes transparency and cooperation requirements for general-purpose AI models. Imposes additional risk management and evaluation obligations for general-purpose models with systemic risks.

Applies to AI developers and deployers whose systems are used in the EU market, regardless of their physical location, with certain exceptions.

Defines regulatory exemptions for free and open-source AI systems, subject to transparency and licensing requirements.

Establishes the European Commission’s AI Office to lead implementation efforts and enforce compliance. Allows significant penalties for violations. Defines additional AI regulatory roles for advisory boards and national-level authorities.

Official name: Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act
Casual name: Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act
Short summary: Defines privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) and instructs the National Science Foundation to support research on them. Directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy to coordinate with NSF, NIST, and the FTC to accelerate PET development and use, and to report to Congress on implementation.
Long summary:
Defines “privacy-enhancing technologies” (PETs) to include methods such as differential privacy, synthetic data, and federated learning.

Instructs the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support PET research by awarding research projects related to privacy preserving technologies including algorithms, machine learning, and other computational processes used to protect privacy when handling data.

Amends (D) of 4(a)(1) of the Cybersecurity Research and Development Act.

Official name: William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology")
Casual name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology")
Short summary: Addresses the research and development of artificial intelligence technologies in the Department of Defense. Establishes a board of advisors for the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center to provide strategic advice and technical expertise on matters relating to the development and use of artificial intelligence. Supports the implementation of ethical and responsible artificial intelligence systems and standards for artificial intelligence.
Long summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to assign roles and responsibilities relating to the research, development, testing, procurement of, requirements for, and operational use of artificial intelligence technologies to appropriate officials within the Department of Defense.

Supports the incorporation of standards for artificial intelligence into the strategies and doctrine of the Department.

Stipulates the roles of the Director of the joint Artificial Intelligence center.

Encourages the systematic evaluation of AI systems.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a board of advisors for the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center with responsibilities like providing strategic advice and expertise to the Secretary and the Director on matters relating to the development and use of artificial intelligence.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to identify a set of no fewer than five use cases of the application of existing artificial intelligence enabled systems to support improved management of enterprise acquisition, personnel, audit, or financial management functions.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to conduct an assessment to determine how the Department can most effectively implement ethically and responsibly developed artificial intelligence.

Requires the secretary to pilot technology development and prototyping activities that leverage commercially available technologies and systems to demonstrate new artificial intelligence enabled capabilities to support the use cases.

Permits the secretary of Defense to establish a steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats, which committee shall develop a strategy for the organizational change, capability development, and technology investments in emerging technologies needed to maintain the technological superiority of the United States military.

Long summary:

Instructs the Secretary to develop a transfer plan with consideration of all appropriate entities, while considering whether the receiving electromagnetic spectrum operations organization should have a unitary structure or hybrid structure.

Requires the Secretary to develop the transfer plan while considering the resources required by the receiving electromagnetic spectrum operations organization to fulfill the responsibilities and functions as well as the results of the evaluations carried out.

Casual name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 247 ("Pilot program on the use of electronic portfolios to evaluate certain applicants for technical positions")
Short summary: Instructs the Secretary of Defense to carry out a pilot program where certain applicants for technical positions within the Department of Defense will be evaluated based partly on each applicant’s electronic portfolio.
Long summary:
Defines the term "technical position" as a Department of Defense position that (1) requires expertise in artificial intelligence, data science, or software development and (2) is eligible for direct hire authority under section 9905 of title 5, United States Code, or section 2358a of title 10, United States Code. 

Instructs the human resources manager of each Department of Defense participating organization to identify a subset of technical positions for which electronic portfolios should be evaluated during the hiring process.

Requires the Human Resources manager to evaluate applicants for such positions by reviewing their best electronic portfolios, as chosen by the applicant.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to the congressional defense committee on the results of the program that describes how electronic portfolios affected the timeliness of technical position hiring, the level of satisfaction with new hires based on electronic portfolio evaluations, and recommends expanding the use of electronic portfolios in the hiring process or making it permanent.

Official name: William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking")
Casual name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking")
Short summary: Instructs the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study on trafficking routes employed by transnational criminals. This emcompasses examining methods for laundering proceeds from trafficking, with a focus on the role of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, in facilitating the laundering of proceedings from trafficking.
Long summary:
Instructs the Comptroller General of the United States to carry out a study in consultation with law enforcement, relevant federal agencies, private sector stakeholders (such as financial institutions, data and technology companies), to investigate major trafficking routes used by transnational criminal organizations and to what extent the trafficking routes are related.

Directs the study to include commonly used methods to launder and move the proceeds of trafficking; the types of suspicious financial activity that are associated with illicit trafficking networks, and how financial institutions identify and report such activity.

Directs the study to include steps financial institutions are taking to detect and prevent bad actors who are laundering the proceeds of illicit trafficking, including data analysis, policies, training procedures, rules, and guidance,

Necessitates the study to include the role those emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital identity technologies, distributed ledger technologies, virtual assets and online marketplaces can play in enabling the laundering of proceeds from trafficking. 

Requires the Comptroller General of the United States to submit a report to the congres, summarizing the results of the study and any recommendations for regulatory action.

Official name: William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts")
Casual name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts")
Short summary: A directive for covered agencies, including the Department of Defense, to employ updated algorithms, data, and AI tools in modernizing their infrastructure for managing Federal spectrum. This involves enhancing efficiency, validation, accuracy, modeling, and monitoring, with a specific emphasis on automated adjustments, collaborative spectrum sharing, and interoperability, while also mandating comprehensive plans, reviews, and oversight to ensure effective implementation and integration of these AI-driven advancements.
Long summary:
Use updated algorithms, data, AI tools, and algorithms to modernize infrastructure. Ways to improve infrastructure include efficiency, validation, accuracy, modeling, and monitoring. The directive aims to enhance covered agencies' capacity to meet mission requirements in congested Federal spectrum environments through the implementation of automated adjustments, the creation of a time-based mechanism for collaborative spectrum sharing among agencies, and fostering collaboration to ensure interoperability. 

Within 240 days of the enactment of this Act, the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information is required to submit to Congress a report outlining a plan for the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to modernize and automate its infrastructure for managing the use of Federal spectrum by covered agencies, with the goal of improving efficiency in spectrum management in ways such as a timeline for implementation, plans for security enhancement, data model improvement, and workflow automation. 

Within one year of the enactment of this Act, the head of each covered agency is required to submit a report to the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information and the Policy and Plans Steering Group outlining a plan to modernize the agency's infrastructure. Each submitted report must include an assessment of their current capabilities, a timeline for completion, management capabilities, agency requirements or restrictions, existing infrastructure, and a plan for safe integration of government data.

The Comptroller General of the United States is mandated to conduct a review of covered agencies' infrastructure within 180 days of the Act's enactment and subsequently oversee the implementation of modernization plans submitted by the Assistant Secretary and covered agencies, providing regular reports and briefings to relevant congressional committees until December 31, 2030. Short summary: After this act is passed, the Director of National Intelligence must submit a detailed report about the production of semiconductors in China. Long summary:
Begins discussing the phrase “appropriate committees of Congress” and what organizations are actually a part of this phrase when benign referred. Also defines the term “legacy semiconductor” in terms of the definition given in another legislation document.

Annually for 3 years after this act is passed, the Director of National Intelligence must submit an unclassified assessment report regarding China’s production of semiconductors through China’s firms and business sectors to the appropriate committees of Congress.

They must discuss Chinese firms’s production of semiconductors that are not legacy conductors and stockpiling efforts of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence")
Short summary: Declares that it is the policy of the United States to ensure AI use does not undermine the integrity of nuclear safeguards or human decision-making with respect to the use of nuclear weapons.
Long summary:
Expresses the sense of Congress that artificial intelligence and machine learning can strengthen strategic communications, improve planning efficiency, and enhance modeling capabilities for stockpile stewardship.

Emphasizes the need for caution to prevent AI from compromising critical strategic assets.

Establishes U.S. policy that AI use should not undermine nuclear safeguards, affect weapon system functionality, or alter the validation of command communications.

Requires positive human actions for nuclear weapon employment decisions by the President to remain intact.

Mandates the Director of the National Security Agency to establish an Artificial Intelligence Security Center (within the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center of NSA) within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Requires the Center to develop guidance to prevent or mitigate counter-artificial intelligence techniques.

Promotes secure artificial intelligence adoption practices for managers of national security systems and the defense industrial base.

Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges")
Short summary: Amends the Intelligence Authorization Act to enhance intelligence community-private sector talent exchanges, focusing on fields like AI.
Long summary:
Amends section 5306 to require public-private talent exchanges in intelligence or counterintelligence to focus on fields including artificial intelligence.

Extends the duration of temporary details for such exchanges from 3 years to 5 years.

Prohibits private-sector employees detailed to the intelligence community from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information.

Clarifies that participation in the exchange program does not create an organizational conflict of interest solely by virtue of involvement.

Requires implementation of systems to address any identified conflicts of interest.

Mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to Congress on the implementation and use of the exchange program, including recommendations for improvements, for three consecutive years.

Requires submittal of a review to congressional defense committees within 30 days of completion.

Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities")
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to study and report on the use of unmanned ground vehicle systems produced by specified foreign adversaries, and prohibits procuring the systems if a national security threat is found.
Long summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to study the use of unmanned ground vehicle systems by the Department of Defense manufactured by certain foreign entities.

Requires submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 180 days, assessing usage, national security threats, and identifying foreign manufacturers.

Calls for the evaluation of cybersecurity risks, technological vulnerabilities, and the foreign entities' military-civil nexus.

Demands an assessment of the feasibility of the Defense Innovation Unit developing a list of U.S. manufacturers.

Mandates an evaluation of whether a prohibition on procuring and operating these systems is advisable for U.S. national security.

Prohibits procurement and operation of these systems by the Department of Defense one year after the report submission, unless deemed in the national interest.

Exempts this prohibition if recommended as not in the best national security interest.

Defines "covered foreign countries" including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles")
Short summary: Requires the Navy to demonstrate large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles by June 2025 and conduct related assessments.
Long summary:
Mandates the Secretary of the Navy to conduct a competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles by June 1, 2025, in coordination with relevant military entities.

Requires evaluation of user feedback on these vehicles as well as vehicles' integration with mission autonomy planning, capability in contested environments, performance attributes, technical maturity, and cost to procure, operate, and sustain.

Permits the use of fiscal year 2025 Navy funds for research, development, and demonstration activities.

Obligates the Secretary of the Navy and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to submit assessments to congressional defense committees by September 1, 2025, which may include recommendations and validation of underwater vehicle requirements.

Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Title XV, Subtitle D ("Artificial Intelligence")

Long summary:
Establishes an initiative to improve the usability of AI systems, that are used by Department of Defense personnel, by considering human factors and cognitive ergonomics. It mandates the development of a guidance plan for their inclusion and evaluation in current and future programs. 

Establishes a program for high-performance computing infrastructure to support advanced AI capabilities, ensuring non-duplication with Department of Energy efforts. The instrument mandates the development of a roadmap that assesses the anticipated compute requirements, security standards, and relevant resources for the infrastructure required to enable advanced AI capabilities. 

Mandates developing a plan for costs and budgeting related to data used for various stages in the AI development and deployment lifecycle. This plan must include budgets for current programs and programs established by the enactment of this Act, as well as, costs related to data procurement, preparation, protection, and analysis. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to evaluate the feasibility of centers of excellence for AI-enabled weapon systems, focusing on national and international collaboration, training of personnel, and best practices. Requires a report and briefing to Congress.

Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture")

Long summary:
Requires, within 180 days, the Secretary of the Navy to provide a forum and resources for industry participation in developing a vendor-agnostic and platform-agnostic modular open systems architecture for maritime unmanned systems.

Directs the Secretary of the Navy to adopt or join a governance model that includes both Government and industry for the maritime unmanned systems standards.

Mandates the implementation of a process for incorporating industry feedback into these standards and aligning them with leading industry practices.

Requires the standards for maritime unmanned systems to be tailored for each relevant Navy program or contract to meet the minimum standards necessary for desired operational capabilities.

Instructs the Secretary of the Navy to label and distribute the standards as open and publicly releasable information to the greatest extent possible.

Requires the group to develop AI strategies and interoperability for intelligence sharing, battlespace awareness, and other defense operations.

Mandates managing AI data security and evaluating defense industrial capabilities for AI integration.

Ensures knowledge and technical data remain under the control of the originating country’s export laws.

Terminates the group on September 30, 2028, unless extended for national security reasons by the Secretary.

Casual name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security")
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct a pilot program for developing AI for national security-related biotechnology applications through public-private partnerships.
Long summary:

Requires collaboration through public-private partnerships to execute the program.

Permits the use of Department of Defense laboratory facilities and computing infrastructure to support biotechnology experimentation and AI model validation.

Stipulates the program's commencement within one year of enactment and its termination five years after starting.

Obligates the Secretary to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees, detailing program progress, data resource assessments, cybersecurity measures, collaboration mechanisms, and AI roles in biotechnology.

Requires the strategy to assess means to increase AI adoption in the DOD's multi-cloud environments and identify opportunities to improve planning on data use and storage, including policies to enforce the protection of government data used for training AI models.

Mandates updating the Department's Human Capital Operating Plan to align with strategic goals and ensure consistent AI terminology.

Sunsets the authority for this initiative five years post-enactment.

Long summary:
Resumes border wall system construction, requiring the Secretary of Homeland Security to restart halted projects and honor previous agreements.

Prohibits the cancellation of contracts related to border wall construction entered into before January 20, 2021.

Requires the lifting of COVID-19 related suspension of entries and imports not earlier than 120 days after the termination of the public health emergency.

Mandates submission of plans to manage possible influxes related to the termination of COVID-19 suspensions.

Disapproves the rule allowing asylum officers to adjudicate credible fear claims, maintaining exclusive authority for immigration judges.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the return of aliens to contiguous territory or detain them for further asylum consideration.

Establishes minimum staffing levels for various immigration and border enforcement offices, including 25,000 U.S. Border Patrol agents.

Ensures funding for sufficient detention facilities to comply with mandatory detention requirements.

Mandates a report within 60 days on how the Department of Homeland Security is mitigating border encounters.

Official name: National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act
Casual name: Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Act
Short summary: Requires the President to develop a national strategy for using microreactors in natural disaster response. Involves consultation with multiple federal agencies and includes assessments, goals, and recommendations for deploying microreactors efficiently and safely, emphasizing technological integration and partnerships.

Official name: Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023
Casual name: Forest Data Modernization Act
Short summary: Amends the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Research Act to integrate AI and advanced technologies, including machine learning, for enhanced forest data collection and analysis.
Long summary:
Amends the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Research Act to include forest carbon in resource assessments.

Updates strategic plan to include consistent data collection protocols, integration of new technologies, and enhanced transparency.

Amends the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 to authorize microwave, LiDAR, hyperspectral, high-resolution remote sensing, and machine learning technologies for forest data analysis.
Tags: Strategies: Governance development

Official name: Know Your App Act
Casual name: Know Your App Act
Short summary: Requires application stores to prominently display the primary country of origin for each application. Allows users to filter or receive disclaimers for apps from concerning countries. Requires the Treasury and Commerce Secretaries to submit to Congress a list of foreign countries that subject app developers to control by the government of the country over content moderation, algorithm design, or user data transfers.
Long summary:
Requires covered companies to publicly list the primary country of origin of each application on the app store page with prominent display.

Mandates that covered companies provide an option to filter out apps from countries of concern and display disclaimers if data could be accessed by a foreign government.

Requires the Treasury and Commerce Secretaries to submit to Congress a list of foreign countries with a national law that subjects the app developers to control by the government of the country over content moderation, algorithm design, or user data transfers. Goes into effect 180 days after the act's enactment.
Tags: Strategies: Government study or report

Official name: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes")
Casual name: Drone R&D Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes")
Short summary: Establishes a program to fund Institutes focusing on unmanned aircraft systems, including AI research. Encourages partnerships, supports interdisciplinary education, and requires data management strategies. Allocates $5 million annually for 2024-2028. Prioritizes merit-based selection and avoids duplicative efforts.
Long summary:
Establishes a program to award financial assistance for creating and supporting a network of National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes.

Requires collaboration among public and private organizations, including Federal agencies, academic institutions, and industry, to form these Institutes.

Mandates the Institutes to focus on economic or social sectors and address ethical, societal, safety, and security implications of unmanned aircraft systems.

Supports interdisciplinary research, education, and workforce development, including broadening participation of underrepresented communities.

Provides funds for managing data sets, developing testbeds, conducting research, and supporting AI and machine learning related to advanced air mobility systems.

Imposes a competitive merit review process for awarding financial assistance and prohibits duplication of efforts.

Authorizes $5 million annually for fiscal years 2024-2028 to support these activities.

Official name: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 909 ("Requirement to Ensure Intelligence Community Directives Appropriately Account for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Tools in Intelligence Products")
Casual name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 909 ("Ensure IC Directives Account for AI and ML Tools in Intelligence Products")
Short summary: Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief Congress on AI and machine learning guidance in intelligence products within 120 days. Determines whether existing directives provide sufficient guidance and whether updates are necessary, including explanations or update plans and timelines.
Long summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief congressional intelligence committees within 120 days on whether current intelligence community directives provide sufficient guidance on the use of AI and machine learning tools in intelligence products.

Mandates the briefing to include a determination of whether Intelligence Community Directives 203 and 206, and other relevant directives, offer adequate guidance on using, sourcing, and providing transparency for AI and machine learning tools.

Requires the Director to assess if these directives need updates to enhance guidance and direction.

Obligates the Director to explain why no updates are needed if deemed sufficient, or to provide a plan and timeline for necessary updates if improvements are required.
Tags: Strategies: Evaluation;Risk factors: Transparency

Official name: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence")
Casual name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 906 ("Next-Generation Microelectronics for AI")
Short summary: Establishes a program to advance microelectronics research supporting AI that focuses on next-generation computing models and overcoming microelectronics challenges. Requires collaboration with government, academia, and industry, and mandates regular congressional briefings on progress.
Long summary:
Establishes a program to advance microelectronics research, overseen by the Director of National Intelligence through the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity.

Focuses research on next-generation computing models, materials, devices, architectures, and algorithms to enhance artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Promotes advancements in computing technologies through multidisciplinary research, encompassing algorithm design, compute capability, generative AI, photonics-based microprocessors, new materials, optical networks, and AI safety for the intelligence community.

Requires active collaboration with government agencies, academic institutions, and private industry.

Authorizes appropriations for contracts, grants, and other transactions to support the program.

Mandates regular briefings to congressional intelligence committees on program progress, partnerships, and future research priorities.

Official name: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System")
Casual name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System")
Short summary: Amends the National Integrated Drought Information System to include AI, machine learning, and cloud technologies for drought monitoring and forecasting. Establishes partnerships for coordinated drought information and updates modeling to probabilistic forecasts.
Long summary:
Amends the National Integrated Drought Information System Act of 2006 to advance and deploy next-generation technologies related to drought, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud technologies.

Requires incorporation of flash drought research and tools to enhance timely response.

Mandates utilization of observational networks and refinement of drought indicators for decision-support products by optimizing data from across the Federal Government.

Establishes memoranda of understanding with the National Mesonet Program to provide coordinated, high-quality, nationwide drought information.

Directs the transition of existing drought products to probabilistic forecasts and incorporation of new dynamical and statistical forecast modeling tools.

Authorizes appropriations increasing annually from $15,000,000 in fiscal year 2024 to $17,000,000 in fiscal year 2028.
Tags: Strategies: Government support;Strategies: Government support: For R&D;Strategies: Convening;Strategies: Government support

Official name: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication")
Casual name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather Risk Communication")
Short summary: Improves NOAA's communication system for hazardous weather risks using social, behavioral, and AI research. Coordinates with governmental and educational partners to ensure timely, consistent public information dissemination.
Long summary:
Amends Section 406 of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act of 2017 to enhance communication about hazardous weather or water events.

Requires the Under Secretary to maintain and improve NOAA's system for communicating risks of hazardous weather or water events to the public.

Mandates the creation of a social, behavioral, risk, communication, and economic sciences program to simplify and improve communication of hazardous weather or water events.

Requires recommendations to be based on the latest social, behavioral, economic, risk, and communications science research, validated using rigorous methods, including AI and machine learning.

Ensures coordination with federal, state, local, tribal, educational, and media partners.

Establishes best practices for timely and consistent communications across public platforms.
Tags: Strategies: Convening

Official name: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices")
Casual name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing")
Short summary: Establishes data standards and infrastructure to support open science and efficient data transfer, including AI for data assimilation. Forms a consortium to advance data assimilation research and workforce development.
Long summary:
Establishes the requirement for the Under Secretary, in collaboration with the weather enterprise, to develop consistent and open data and metadata standards to support open science.

Instructs the establishment of a program to advance data assimilation methods, including AI and machine learning, and the creation of a university consortium to address research challenges in data assimilation.

Official name: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 116(f) ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network")
Casual name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 116(f) ("Algal Bloom Observing Network")
Short summary: Integrates Federal, State, regional, and local capabilities to establish a national network for harmful algal bloom monitoring, incorporating artificial intelligence. Establishes a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center for data integration and ecological forecasting support.
Long summary:
Amends Section 606 of the Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Research and Control Act to establish a national harmful algal bloom observing network.

Requires the Under Secretary, via NCCOS and IOOS, to integrate Federal, State, regional, and local observing capabilities.

Mandates the use of emerging technologies and data integration methods, including artificial intelligence, for monitoring, detecting, and forecasting harmful algal blooms.

Instructs the IOOS Program Office to coordinate with NCCOS for observations, data integration, and information dissemination.

Establishes a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center to integrate, disseminate, and support ecological forecasting.

Official name: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization")
Casual name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization")
Short summary: Requires the Under Secretary and Secretary of Energy to leverage AI and machine learning for NOAA's missions. Establishes centers of excellence for AI advancements. Mandates a report evaluating initiative effectiveness and needs for computing collaboration with the Department of Energy.
Long summary:
Amends the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act to mandate collaboration between the Under Secretary and the Secretary of Energy in leveraging high-performance computing and AI for advanced weather forecasting.

Requires a competitive, merit-reviewed process for initiative applications, including Federal agencies, National Laboratories, and higher education institutions.

Mandates coordination of AI and computing research across NOAA to avoid duplication and enhance predictive analysis.

Supports model comparison, data sharing, interagency collaboration, long-term data archiving, agile computing decisions, workforce development, and compliance with federal research security requirements. 

Directs sharing of model innovations through community-based activities and interagency coordination.

Authorizes leveraging AI to enhance NOAA’s computing infrastructure for critical missions.

Allows establishment of centers of excellence for AI and machine learning in weather forecasting.

Permits multi-year contracts for high-performance and cloud computing systems.

Requires a report to Congress evaluating the initiative’s effectiveness and future computing needs within two years.

Official name: Counseling for Career Choice Act
Casual name: Counseling for Career Choice Act
Short summary: Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to enhance career counseling, including using AI for career development.
Long summary:
Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to expand career counseling opportunities.

Requires career counseling programs to leverage resources and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Official name: New York A7106
Casual name: New York A7106 ("PAID Act")
Short summary: Amends election law to require disclosure of synthetic media in use in printed or digital political communications by writing or speaking, "This political communication was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence." Defines synthetic media as AI-modified text, image, video, or sound.
Long summary:
Amends the election law to mandate disclosure of synthetic media in political communications.

Requires disclosure for printed or digital political communications to display, "This political communication was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence."

Mandates non-printed or digital political communications, such as radio, to clearly display or speak the same statement.

Defines "synthetic media" as any form of media, including text, image, video, or sound, created or modified using AI algorithms.

Sets the effective date of this act to January 1, 2024.

Official name: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities")
Casual name: Drone R&D Act, Title VI ("DOE Activities")
Short summary: Advances unmanned aircraft systems and AI technologies through research, education, and financial support. Establishes data management strategies and interagency coordination. Allocates funding from fiscal years 2024 to 2028 for eligible entities to enhance DOE missions.
Long summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Energy to execute a cross-cutting research, development, and demonstration program for unmanned aircraft system (UAS) technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Requires coordination across relevant DOE offices, including the Artificial Intelligence Technology Office.

Requires the Secretary to set goals for unmanned aircraft systems research; build on existing research efforts; provide undergraduate and graduate training across AI, machine learning, sensing, materials, and energy technologies; establish a robust, interoperable data management strategy; and support dedicated institutes to advance unmanned aircraft systems and DOE mission priorities.

Awards financial assistance for research in both fundamental S&T areas and applications.

Mandates the Secretary to promote technology transfer by partnering with industry,
make available DOE research facilities and high-performance computing infrastructure, and coordinate with other federal departments to avoid duplication and ensure complementary activities.

Authorizes appropriations totaling $276,282,638 from fiscal years 2024 to 2028.

Official name: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities")
Casual name: Drone R&D Act, Title IV ("NSF Activities")
Short summary: Supports research and education on AI integration into advanced air mobility and unmanned aircraft, encouraging ethical use, cybersecurity, data management, and workforce development. Establishes partnerships and coordinates with agencies to enhance domestic development, allocating specific funds through 2028.
Long summary:
Mandates the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support research and STEM education in advanced air mobility and unmanned aircraft systems.

Supports fundamental research on technologies including AI, safety, autonomous control, materials, and communications systems.

Funds research on practical applications such as weather prediction, disaster response, and infrastructure monitoring.

Supports research on data modeling, validation, security, and ethical use, including privacy concerns.

Encourages middle and high school STEM education related to unmanned aircraft systems through curriculum development and student engagement activities.

Promotes undergraduate and graduate education through curriculum development, hands-on research opportunities, and scholarships.

Develops a skilled technical workforce, including veterans, through national centers and community college programs.

Facilitates public-private partnerships and interagency coordination to avoid research duplication.

Authorizes appropriations increasing from $50 million in 2024 to nearly $61 million in 2028.

Official name: Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act
Casual name: Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act
Short summary: Establishes a cybersecurity clearinghouse for the food and agriculture industry. Requires consolidation of cybersecurity recommendations and consultations with various stakeholders. Mandates a study on federal efforts to improve industry cybersecurity.
Long summary:
Defines key terms for NTIA Food and Agriculture Cybersecurity Clearinghouse, including "cybersecurity risk" and "food and agriculture industry."

Establishes a food and agriculture cybersecurity clearinghouse within the NTIA to provide publicly available online resources focused on cybersecurity for the food and agriculture industry.

Requires the clearinghouse to be publicly available online and provide current cybersecurity resources focused on the food and agriculture industry, a support request mechanism, regularly updated FAQ section, and targeted materials for small and non-technical users on critical cybersecurity protections.

Requires the Assistant Secretary to work with relevant agencies to consolidate public and private sector best practices into a set of voluntary cybersecurity recommendations for the food and agriculture industry, including risk-based and cybersecurity-informed engineering, system control planning, protection measures, threat defenses, ransomware response, and data integrity recommendations.

Instructs the Assistant Secretary to consult with private sector, federal agencies, trade groups, and civil society organizations in implementing the clearinghouse.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report on federal efforts to improve cybersecurity in the food and agriculture industry, evaluating effectiveness, resources, coordination, and potential risks of coordinated attacks.

Sunsets the section seven years after enactment.

Official name: North Carolina SB 460
Casual name: North Carolina SB 460 ("Automation and Workforce")
Short summary: Establishes a Study Committee on Automation and the Workforce to assess the impact of automation technologies, including AI, on North Carolina's workforce, especially low-income and minority workers. Requires biennial reports with recommendations to the Governor and legislature.
Long summary:
Establishes the Study Committee on Automation and the Workforce to analyze the impact of automation on North Carolina's workforce, with a focus on low-income and minority workers.

Requires the Committee to review the current and future impact of artificial intelligence, industrial robotics, self-service systems and productivity software on the State's low-income workforce.

Requires the Committee to identify the education, training, retraining, and skill-development needed to help low-income workers adapt to automation and reduce job displacement

Requires the Committee to evaluate how the State and employers can work together to sustain and create employment opportunities in response to the current and future impacts of automation.

Requires the Committee to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and Joint Legislative Commission on Governmental Operations before the 2025 General Assembly and biennially thereafter.

Official name: American Privacy Rights Act of 2024, Sec. 114-5
Casual name: American Privacy Rights Act of 2024, Sec. 114-5
Short summary: Establishes a pilot program to promote privacy-enhancing technologies like homomorphic encryption and federated learning. Requires development of a petition process and an auditing system for oversight. Mandates ongoing audits and allows withdrawal for non-compliance. Provides liability limitations for compliant participants.
Long summary:
Establishes a pilot program to encourage private sector use of privacy-enhancing technologies within one year of the Act's enactment to protect covered data.

Requires the Commission to develop a petition process for entities to join the pilot program and implement an auditing system using privacy-enhancing technologies for enforcement purposes.

Mandates ongoing audits of participating entities to ensure compliance with privacy-enhancing technologies.

Allows covered entities deemed compliant to be considered in compliance with section 109, with a rebuttable presumption in certain legal actions.

Obligates the Comptroller General to study the pilot program's progress and effectiveness, with an initial briefing and a final report to Congress.

Creates a new bureau within the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce the title with experts, including technologists experienced with AI.

Establishes a Privacy and Security Victims Relief Fund for consumer redress and technological research.

Requires the FTC to report to Congress on investigations and future plans related to the title.

Official name: Comment Integrity and Management Act of 2024
Casual name: Comment Integrity and Management Act
Short summary: Amends the E-Government Act to require verification of human origin for electronic comments, identify mass and AI-generated comments, and allow agencies to post representative samples. Directs OMB to issue guidance for managing these comments and mandates policy updates.
Long summary:
Amends the E-Government Act of 2002 to improve the handling of mass and computer-generated comments in the regulatory review process.

Requires agencies to verify whether electronic comments are submitted by humans.

Mandates agencies to identify and label mass comments and allows agencies to post representative samples of these comments.

Directs the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidance on verifying human submissions and managing mass comments, including the use of technology tools.

Obliges agencies to establish and publicly post policies on handling computer-generated and mass comments within one year of enactment.

Compels the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to report on the identification and impact of computer-generated comments within two years.
Tags: Strategies: Government study or report

Official name: Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats
Casual name: S. 2346 (Public Health Response to AI)
Short summary: Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and report to Congress a strategy addressing AI misuse threats to national health security. Involves public health preparedness, identifying gaps, and mitigating risks like biological weapons.
Long summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop a strategy for public health preparedness and response to artificial intelligence (AI) threats within 180 days of enactment with the following requirements: a framework for public health preparedness and response to mitigate the risks of misuse of artificial intelligence; an outline of the duties, functions, and preparedness goals for which the Secretary is responsible; gaps in public health capabilities and strategies to address these gaps and strengthen emergency preparedness against AI threats; strategies to mitigate risks, such as the development of biological weapons and treatment-resistant viruses and bacteria.

Requires the strategy to be submitted to relevant congressional committees without compromising national security.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to integrate this AI threat strategy into the broader federal response to public health emergencies.
